claim: silent-discard: `resolve_control` maps any `kv::get` error (corrupt or unreadable kv.json) to `Control::Allowed`, so a stored `lookout.allow_control=false` gate silently opens (documented fail-open, but no notice is shown).
reason: The doc comment on `resolve_control` says outright that an unreadable store leaves control on, because the gate exists to stop an accident, not an attacker. A convenience toggle that fails open quietly is a deliberate design choice, not a silent-discard bug.

claim: silent-discard: `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` discards the draw error, then clears `dirty` and stamps `last_draw`, so a persistently failing terminal write leaves a frozen screen with no report.
reason: At line 167, `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` drops the io::Error without a comment, a log line or an exit. It then clears `dirty` and stamps `last_draw`, so if the terminal write keeps failing the screen stays frozen and the operator gets no error.

claim: silent-discard: `Err(_other) => Ok(())` in `reconcile` drops every non-Closed `ListFlock` failure with no log or notice, so a persistently failing poll leaves a stale flock that looks live.
reason: The discard is deliberate and documented in the doc comment above `reconcile`, and `reconcile` is not a recurring poll: it runs only after a `Dropped` or `Lagged` event, which the UI has already received as `Msg::Event` or `Msg::BusLagged`, so there is no 'persistently failing poll'; the one real gap is that the UI is never told the repair itself failed.

claim: silent-discard: `Some(Err(_)) | None` drops a keyboard event-stream I/O error and retires the input arm for good, so lookout stops responding to keys and nothing tells the operator why.
reason: Retiring the arm is deliberate, but `keys_done` is used nowhere else: the error is thrown away, no status reaches the screen, and the loop keeps running without input. In raw mode Ctrl-C is just a key, so the operator can't quit and never learns why.

claim: silent-discard: `secrets::get(..).ok().flatten()` turns an I/O, parse or lock error reading `secrets.json` into "no value", so a failed reveal looks the same as a missing slot.
reason: `stored_value` maps any `secrets::get` error to `None`, and `on_revealed` (reveal_secret.rs) just returns on `None` with no message, so an unreadable, corrupt or locked `secrets.json` looks exactly like a slot that has disappeared. The doc comment says this is deliberate, but it still throws the error away.

claim: silent-discard: `value.filter(|_| gate_open)` plus `else { return }` folds a failed store read into "nothing to show" after `pending_reveal` was cleared, so a `v` press whose read errored shows nothing and raises no notice.
reason: The `Msg::Revealed.value` docs (msg.rs:356) say `None` means either "the slot no longer resolves" or "the store would not read". `on_revealed` clears `pending_reveal`, then returns silently on `None` without setting a notice, so a failed store read after `v` looks the same as having nothing to show.

claim: silent-discard: `read_to_string(&paths.daemon_config).ok()` and `DaemonConfig::load(..).is_ok_and(..)` turn an unreadable or malformed `shep.toml` into `allow_read = false`, so the reveal gate reads as closed with no error naming the config problem (fail-closed by design).
reason: Closing the reveal gate when shep.toml can't be read or parsed is the intended fail-closed security behaviour, and a missing file correctly falls back to defaults through `load(None)`; a malformed shep.toml also shows up as a config error when the shepherd loads it, so the pane staying silent is at most a UX nit, not a defect.

claim: silent-discard: `pane.environment().unwrap_or_default()` turns a missing environment tab into an empty-string environment that goes into the `SecretEdit` write, whereas `confirm_secret_delete` refuses in the same case.
reason: `environment()` returns `None` before the first load (secrets_pane.rs:103). Write_secret then sends an empty-string environment in the `SecretEdit`, while `confirm_secret_delete` (delete_secret.rs:61) returns `Effect::None` in the same case.

claim: silent-discard: `Terminate::install().ok()` swallows a failure to install the SIGTERM handler, so lookout runs without graceful termination and never says so.
reason: On Unix, `Terminate::install()` fails only if tokio's signal driver cannot register, which is practically unreachable inside lookout's running runtime; the `.ok()` into an `Option` is a deliberate optional-handler pattern, and printing a warning while the TUI owns the screen would corrupt it.

claim: silent-discard: `let _ = copy_to_clipboard(..)` throws away the stdout write/flush error while the pane words the copy as "sent", so a failed copy is never surfaced (a comment says this is intentional).
reason: The discard at crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/ui_event_loop.rs:509 is a documented design choice: the only failure is a stdout write error, which means the TUI's own terminal is broken and there's nowhere to report it, and the pane deliberately says "sent", not "copied", because OSC 52 can't confirm the copy arrived anyway.

claim: silent-discard: `serde_json::to_value(config).ok()...unwrap_or_default()` swallows a serialization failure into an empty value map, so the sheep config pane would show every field unset and offer edits against that (very unlikely to fire).
reason: The code at fields.rs:74 does turn a to_value failure, or a non-object result, into an empty map with no log or error, so the pane would show every field unset; it is just very unlikely to fire because a derived Serialize config struct almost always serializes to an object.

claim: silent-discard: `pane.value("instances").parse().unwrap_or(1)` swallows a parse error into a made-up instance count of 1 that the dialog row shows as fact (the comment argues it cannot fail).
reason: `close_offer` builds the dialog only for a `PaneTarget::Sheep`, and a sheep pane's `values` map comes from a serialised `AppConfig` whose `instances` field is a `u32`, so `value("instances")` always renders a plain integer and the `unwrap_or(1)` fallback can't be reached.

claim: a key-source `Some(Err(_))` (crossterm read error) is discarded and permanently retires the keyboard arm with no notice or log, so the dashboard silently stops accepting input, including `q` (deliberate per the comment, but with no user-visible signal).
reason: At ui_event_loop.rs:191, `Some(Err(_))` sets `keys_done = true` and drops the error without logging it or telling the user, so after a crossterm read error the dashboard keeps redrawing but ignores every key, `q` included, and only SIGTERM or Ctrl-C (SIGINT) will stop it.

claim: `reconcile` maps every non-`Closed` `flock.flock()` error to `Ok(())` with no `Msg` or notice, so a persistently failing poll (timeout, RPC or protocol error) leaves the dashboard on stale rows with the link still shown Live.
reason: `reconcile` runs on the periodic ticker (line 174), and every non-`Closed` error returns `Ok(())` without sending a `Msg`. While the event subscription stays alive, repeated poll failures such as timeouts or protocol errors never reach the UI, so the rows go stale and nothing marks the link as degraded.

claim: silent-discard: `ConfigPane::dog` turns a `dogs.toml` section that fails `toml::Table` parsing (`.ok()` then `unwrap_or_default()`) into an empty value map, so a broken section opens with every field "(unset)" and the operator only finds out after editing.
reason: The daemon's `dog_section` (shep-daemon/src/dogs/config.rs:31) parses the whole `dogs.toml` through `DogsConfig::load` and returns `DogError::Config` if the file is broken, so the pane only ever gets a section from a file that already parsed; the `.ok()`/`unwrap_or_default()` path can't hide a broken section.

claim: `Terminate::install().ok()` silently drops a failed SIGTERM handler install, so SIGTERM is never handled and terminal restore and clean shutdown are skipped with no warning.
reason: At ui_event_loop.rs:57, `.ok()` discards the install error without logging it, unlike the bark, metrics and serve callers, which report it on stderr and bail. If the install fails, no handler is registered and SIGTERM's default action kills lookout without restoring the terminal. In practice the install almost never fails, so severity is low.

claim: `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` ignores a draw error and still sets `dirty = false` and stamps `last_draw`, so a failed frame is not retried until the next change.
reason: At `ui_event_loop.rs:167` the result of `terminal.draw` is thrown away, then `dirty = false` and `last_draw` are set anyway, so a failed frame is never redrawn until some other event marks the screen dirty again.

claim: `handle.await.ok().flatten()` discards a `spawn_blocking` join failure (a panic in the reveal read) and turns it into "no value", so the operator cannot tell a failed reveal from a gone slot (deliberate per the comment).
reason: The comment at the site documents this as a deliberate design choice: a panicked reveal and a vanished slot both leave nothing to show, and a notice naming a panic gives the operator nothing to act on, so dropping the join error to None is intended behaviour, not a defect.

claim: `resolve_control` sends every result other than `Ok(Some("false"))`, including a kv read `Err`, to `Control::Allowed`, so an unreadable store silently re-enables stop/restart/reload for an operator who set `lookout.allow_control=false` (documented fail-open).
reason: The behavior is real but deliberate: the doc comment at crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/entry.rs:147-153 says an unreadable store leaves control on because the gate exists to stop accidents, not attackers, so this is the documented design, not a defect.

claim: the `copy_to_clipboard` `io::Result` is discarded (`let _ =`), so a failed stdout write for a revealed secret's OSC 52 copy is never reported to the operator (deliberate per the comment).
reason: The discard is intentional and documented: stdout is the TUI's own terminal, so a failed write there leaves nowhere to report the error, and the pane already says the value was sent rather than that it arrived.

claim: `on_revealed` returns silently when `value` is `None`, clearing `pending_reveal` with no notice, so a failed secret read after `v` leaves the operator with no explanation.
reason: `stored_value` folds both a vanished slot and a store that fails to read into `None` (msg.rs:356), and `on_revealed` clears `pending_reveal` and returns without setting `self.notice`; the only comment justifying silence (ui_event_loop.rs:358) covers join panics, not read failures, so a failed read after `v` shows the operator nothing.

claim: `ConfigPane::dog` drops the `toml::Table` parse error via `.ok()`/`unwrap_or_default()`, so an unparsable dog section opens as an all-`(unset)` form with no notice, and the failure only surfaces later in the write path.
reason: The daemon's `dog_section` (crates/shep-daemon/src/dogs/config.rs:39-47) parses `dogs.toml` with shep-core's `DogsConfig::load` and toml_edit before replying, and returns an error for a broken file. So the TOML that reaches `ConfigPane::dog` has already parsed, and the dropped parse error in the pane can't happen through the real call path.

claim: `secrets::get(..).ok().flatten()` drops a read error on `secrets.json` (corrupt, locked or unreadable) and returns `None`, so a failed reveal looks the same as an empty slot.
reason: `stored_value` turns every `secrets::get` error into `None` (its doc comment says this on purpose), and `on_revealed` (reveal_secret.rs:126) just returns on `None` without setting any status, so a corrupt, locked or unreadable `secrets.json` gives the operator the same silent no-op as a slot that has gone.

claim: discarded-error: `resolve_control` matches `_ => Control::Allowed`, so an `Err` from `kv::get` (unreadable or corrupt kv.json) silently turns off a `lookout.allow_control=false` read-only gate (fails open; the doc comment says this is deliberate).
reason: The fail-open is a documented design choice: the doc comment says the gate stops an accident, not an attacker, and `--read-only` stays as the hard gate, so the error isn't silently discarded by mistake.

claim: discarded-error: `Some(Err(_))` from the key stream is dropped and only sets `keys_done = true`, so a terminal input error silently kills all keyboard input with no notice or log.
reason: At line 191 the arm retires on purpose so the loop doesn't spin, but the error is dropped with no log, status line or exit, so the lookout stays on screen with a dead keyboard and, in raw mode, Ctrl-C can't quit it — only SIGTERM can.

claim: discarded-error: `handle.await.ok().flatten()` swallows a `spawn_blocking` join error (panic or cancel) during the secret reveal, so a failed reveal shows no value and no notice.
reason: The swallow is deliberate and documented in the comment right above it (ui_event_loop.rs:358-361): a join failure is meant to read as no value, the same as a slot that is gone, because a panic notice gives the operator nothing to act on.

claim: discarded-error: `reconcile` maps every non-`Closed` `flock.flock()` failure to `Ok(())`, so a failing ListFlock poll is dropped with no notice and no log, and the dashboard can stay stale while looking live.
reason: `reconcile` (link.rs:226) is called only as a repair after a `Dropped` or `Lagged` bus event. When that repair's `flock()` call fails with anything other than `Closed`, the error is swallowed with no log and no message to the UI. The connection stays up, so the view keeps the state from before the lost events and still looks live. The doc comment gives the reason for not propagating the error, but it doesn't justify giving no notice at all.

claim: `requests.try_send(Sent::Lambs { id })` ignores both `Full` and `Closed`, so if the link task is gone the lamb fetch is lost with no signal and the pane can stay "not read yet" (deliberate for `Full`, not for `Closed`).
reason: At ui_event_loop.rs:128, `let _ = requests.try_send(Sent::Lambs { id })` throws away `Closed` as well as `Full`, and the comment only explains the `Full` case; the `Effect::Send` arm at line 256 and `send_batch` both report `Closed`, so a lamb fetch lost to a dead link task sends no signal, though the impact is low if a closed link already shows as disconnected elsewhere in the lookout.

claim: discarded-error: `secrets::get(..).ok().flatten()` turns a secret-store read or parse failure into `None`, which the reveal treats the same as "slot gone", so a broken `secrets.json` is never surfaced.
reason: The doc comment at secrets.rs:161 says outright that `None` covers a store that will not read. The pane model already carries an `unreadable` field that surfaces a broken store when the model is built, so collapsing it to `None` in the on-demand reveal read is a documented design choice, not a lost error.

claim: discarded-error: `let _ = copy_to_clipboard(..)` drops the stdout write error, so a failed OSC 52 copy of a secret gives the operator no signal that nothing was sent.
reason: The discard is deliberate and commented at ui_event_loop.rs:504-507: a stdout write failure means the TUI's own output is broken, so there is nowhere to report it, and the pane already says the value was sent, not that it arrived.

claim: discarded-error: `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` ignores a draw error, so a persistently failing terminal leaves the loop running with a frozen screen and no report.
reason: At crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/ui_event_loop.rs:167, `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` throws away the io::Error. Nothing else reports it or ends the loop, so if the terminal keeps failing, the loop keeps running with a frozen screen and no report.

claim: discarded-error: `Msg::Revealed.value` is `None` when the store would not read, but `on_revealed` clears `pending_reveal` and returns with no notice, so an unreadable secrets store makes `v` do nothing and hides the failure.
reason: `Msg::Revealed.value` is documented as `None` when "the store would not read" (msg.rs:356-357), and `on_revealed` (reveal_secret.rs:125-127) clears `pending_reveal` and returns with no `Notice`, so an unreadable store makes `v` do nothing; the only stated reason for silence (ui_event_loop.rs:359-362) covers a join panic, not an I/O failure the operator could fix.

claim: discarded-error: `Classifier::new` uses `LevelMatcher::compile(rules).ok()`, so an invalid declared level rule is dropped silently and the feed falls back to the built-in reading (the doc says `normalize` makes this unreachable, so low impact).
reason: The fallback is deliberate and documented at level.rs:79-83: `normalize()` rejects rules that won't compile before they can be stored, so this path can't be reached, and if it were, falling back to `level_of` is the stated design choice, not a lost error.

claim: discarded-error: `read_to_string(&paths.daemon_config).ok()` collapses an unreadable or unparsable `shep.toml` into `allow_read = false`; it fails closed, but the pane never says why reveal is denied.
reason: When `shep.toml` can't be read, or `DaemonConfig::load` fails to parse it, `allow_read` is set to false without any message, and the pane header (`pane_chrome.rs:33`) then shows `[secrets] allow_read = false in shep.toml`. That misstates the operator's config instead of reporting the read or parse error; it fails closed, so it is a diagnosability bug, not a security hole.

claim: discarded-error: `Terminate::install().ok()` silently discards a SIGTERM handler install failure, so the loop runs without graceful-shutdown handling and never reports it.
reason: At `ui_event_loop.rs:57`, `Terminate::install().ok()` throws away the error with no comment and no log, so lookout keeps running without SIGTERM handling and nobody is told; the bark and metrics dogs (`dog/bark/event_loop.rs:44`, `dog/metrics/mod.rs:181`) handle the same failure by printing it to stderr, but lookout's degraded mode is never surfaced (the OS almost never refuses this handler, so the impact is low).

claim: an unrecognised `Response` from `ListFlock` becomes `Ok(Vec::new())`, which `reconcile` forwards as an empty `Msg::Snapshot`, so a shepherd reply this build doesn't know can blank the flock with no error shown.
reason: At `source.rs:161`, `ClientFlock::flock` turns any `Response` other than `Flock` into `Ok(Vec::new())`, and `reconcile` (`link.rs:218`) sends every `Ok` as a `Msg::Snapshot`, so an unknown reply blanks the flock with no error shown, while real errors keep the last snapshot (`link.rs:225-226`).

claim: discarded-error: `ConfigPane::dog` runs `parse::<toml::Table>().ok()...unwrap_or_default()`, so an unparseable dog section opens as an empty pane of "(unset)" values with no notice, and the parse error only appears at write time.
reason: The only production caller, `dog_pane.rs:38`, gets its text from the daemon's `dog_section` (`crates/shep-daemon/src/dogs/config.rs:31`). That function returns an error for an invalid `dogs.toml`, and the lookout shows that error as a notice. The section it does return is re-rendered from a parsed `toml_edit` document, so it always parses and the `.ok()` fallback cannot hide a real parse error.

claim: `Some(Err(_))` from the key stream sets `keys_done` with no notice, so a single input read error permanently disables the keyboard, including `q`, and only SIGTERM can then exit.
reason: The behaviour is real and deliberate: the comment at lines 187-190 treats a key-stream error as permanent and retires the arm so it cannot spin. Whether a crossterm `EventStream` error can be transient, which is the only case where silently losing the keyboard and `q` is a bug, isn't settled by this code.

claim: `_ => Control::Allowed` swallows a `kv::get` error, so an unreadable or corrupt `kv.json` re-enables control after the operator set `lookout.allow_control false`.
reason: The behavior is deliberate and documented at entry.rs:152-153: an unreadable KV store leaves control on because the gate exists to stop accidents, not attackers.

claim: `Err(_other) => Ok(())` drops every failed poll except a closed connection (timeouts, decode and protocol errors included), so a poll that always fails leaves a stale flock on screen with nothing surfaced.
reason: `reconcile` at `link.rs:226` silently swallows every non-`Closed` error, including timeouts, decode and protocol failures. It only runs as a repair after `Dropped`/`Lagged`, so a failed repair leaves the pre-gap flock on screen with no message sent to the UI, even though the doc comment calls this deliberate.

claim: `let _ = terminal.draw(...)` drops the draw error and still sets `dirty = false` and `last_draw`, so a dead terminal keeps looping silently.
reason: At line 167, `let _ = terminal.draw(...)` throws away the error and still clears `dirty` and sets `last_draw`; if the terminal dies, the failed key stream only sets `keys_done`, so nothing ends the loop except SIGTERM or the link and it keeps running without output (low severity, because clearing `dirty` at least stops a tight retry spin).

claim: discarded-error: `pane.environment().unwrap_or_default()` turns a missing environment tab into "" and builds an `Effect::WriteSecret` with an empty environment instead of refusing; likely unreachable because the tab index is clamped on reload (low confidence).
reason: Typing only starts when `pane.model.environments` is non-empty (write_secret.rs:23), and `tab` is clamped to that list on reload, so `environment()` returns `Some` whenever this branch runs; the `unwrap_or_default` is a harmless fallback rather than a reachable discarded error.

claim: `handle.await.ok().flatten()` discards a `JoinError`, so a panicked reveal task reads as "no value".
reason: The discard is deliberate and documented in the comment right above it (ui_event_loop.rs:358-361): a join failure is meant to read as no value, because the operator has nothing to act on.

claim: `let _ = copy_to_clipboard(...)` discards the stdout write error, and `dirty` is set as if the copy went out.
reason: The discard is deliberate and documented at ui_event_loop.rs:504-507 (a broken stdout pipe leaves nothing sensible to do, and the pane only claims 'sent', not 'arrived'); `dirty` just triggers a redraw and says nothing about whether the copy succeeded.

claim: `read_to_string(...).ok()` plus `is_ok_and` turns an unreadable or unparseable `shep.toml` into `allow_read = false`, so reveal is refused with no reason given.
reason: At secrets.rs:144-145 a shep.toml that is missing, unreadable or fails to parse collapses to `allow_read = false`, so the pane shows `[secrets] allow_read = false` and the refusal tells the operator to turn on `allow_read`, even if the file already sets it to true; failing closed is correct, but the reason shown is wrong, not missing, and the parse error is never surfaced.

claim: `secrets::get(...).ok().flatten()` folds a store read error into "no value", so the operator can't tell a failed read from an empty slot.
reason: `stored_value` turns a `secrets::get` error into `None`, and `on_revealed` treats `None` by returning without any message, so a failed store read looks the same as a slot that has gone (the doc comment says this is intended, but the operator still gets no signal).

claim: `let _ = msgs.send(Msg::Retrying { attempt }).await;` ignores a closed UI channel and keeps sleeping and re-dialling, unlike the `Relinked` send at line 127, which returns.
reason: When the UI channel is closed, the `Retrying` send's error is thrown away, so the task keeps sleeping with backoff and re-dialling until it runs out of `RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS`, then returns after the `Frozen` send; the `Relinked` send at line 127 returns straight away, so the two paths are inconsistent, though the wasted work is capped rather than endless.

claim: `Terminate::install().ok()` discards the signal-handler install error, so SIGTERM handling is silently absent.
reason: The `.ok()` is on purpose: the None arm at ui_event_loop.rs:175-182 is commented and never completes, so a failed install falls back to having no SIGTERM handling. Nothing is logged, unlike bark, metrics and serve, which report the error and exit. That fits a TUI running on the alternate screen, and install almost never fails, so whether this is a defect or an accepted best-effort fallback is a design call.

claim: a dog's `section.parse::<toml::Table>().ok()` failure becomes an empty values map, so a malformed `dogs.toml` section shows as defaults in the pane with no error.
reason: The daemon's `dog_section` (crates/shep-daemon/src/dogs/config.rs:31) returns `DogError::Config` whenever `dogs.toml` is malformed, and it only sends back a section it has already parsed and re-rendered, so the string the pane receives is always valid TOML and the `.ok()` fallback cannot hide a malformed file.

claim: `let _ = requests.try_send(Sent::Lambs { id })` drops a full or closed channel result, so a lamb fetch is silently skipped.
reason: The drop is deliberate and commented at ui_event_loop.rs:125-127: a full channel means a request is already queued, so the skipped lamb fetch shows as "not read yet" and nothing is lost silently.

claim: `let _ = polls.try_send(())` drops the result, so an `r` refresh is silently lost when the poll channel is full or closed.
reason: Discarding the result is deliberate and documented: when the channel is full, a poll is already queued, so the `r` still gets serviced; when it is closed, the link has ended and the reducer already refuses `r` once the link is `Lost`.

claim: `restore()` discards all three terminal-restore errors (`let _` at lines 30–32); documented and intentional for the panic path, but a failed restore is never reported.
reason: Swallowing the errors is a documented, deliberate choice: `restore()` runs from the panic hook and `Drop`, where returning early on an error would skip the remaining restore steps, and a broken terminal leaves nowhere reliable to report the failure.

claim: `serde_json::to_value(config).ok()` turns a serialisation failure into empty values, so the sheep pane shows every field unset.
reason: `config` is an `AppConfig` with a derived `Serialize`, and `serde_json::to_value` only fails on non-string map keys or a custom serializer error, so the `.ok()` fallback cannot be reached in practice. I did not check every nested field type for such maps, so this is a code-reading judgment, not a proof.

claim: a key-source error (`Some(Err(_))`) is discarded and permanently retires the keyboard arm with no notice, so the dashboard stops responding to keys while it keeps drawing
reason: The `Some(Err(_)) | None` arm at ui_event_loop.rs:191 discards the error and sets `keys_done` on purpose to prevent a spin, but the loop keeps drawing with no notice. In raw mode Ctrl-C arrives as a key, so the dashboard can no longer be quit from the keyboard; breaking out of the loop or showing a notice would avoid both the spin and the silent hang.

claim: the `link` JoinHandle is never awaited, so a panic in `run_link` is discarded; the UI then sees `msgs.recv() == None` and freezes silently, though `ui_event_loop.rs:198` claims that only happens on abort
reason: Panics unwind rather than abort here (the workspace deliberately does not set `panic = "abort"`), so a panic in the spawned `run_link` is caught into the `link` JoinHandle, which `entry.rs` only ever `abort()`s and never awaits. The dropped `msg_tx` then shows up as `None` at `ui_event_loop.rs:198`, whose comment wrongly says that only happens on abort, and the lookout keeps showing a stale frame with no error.

claim: `Err(_other) => Ok(())` drops every non-`Closed` poll error, so a persistently failing `ListFlock` leaves stale rows on screen with no banner or state change
reason: The code is at `crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/link.rs:226`, not `frames/build/link.rs`. There, `reconcile` drops every non-`Closed` error from `flock()` without sending any `Msg`. If `ListFlock` keeps failing while the connection stays open, the subscription never ends and nothing moves the lookout off its last snapshot, so the stale rows stay on screen with no banner. The doc comment only argues that a single failed round trip should be ignored; it doesn't cover repeated failures.

claim: `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` discards a draw error, then clears `dirty` and stamps `last_draw`, so a failed frame is never retried or reported
reason: At `ui_event_loop.rs:167`, `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` drops the `io::Error`, then sets `dirty = false` and stamps `last_draw` with nothing logged. The nearby `let _` discards each carry a comment explaining why they are safe; this one has none. So a failed frame stays unretried until another event marks the screen dirty, and a persistently broken terminal fails silently instead of ending the loop.

claim: `Terminate::install().ok()` discards the SIGTERM handler failure, so a later SIGTERM takes the default action and leaves the terminal in raw mode and the alternate screen
reason: If `Terminate::install()` fails, `.ok()` turns the error into `None` and nothing registers a SIGTERM handler, so SIGTERM keeps its default action and kills the process before the terminal restore runs; tokio's `signal(SIGTERM)` almost never fails in a runtime with signals enabled, so this is a real but low-likelihood gap.

claim: an unreadable `kv.json` falls through `_ => Control::Allowed`, so a corrupt store silently overrides an operator's `allow_control false` (documented as deliberate fail-open)
reason: The behavior is real, but the doc comment at entry.rs:147-153 says an unreadable store leaves control on by design ("the gate stops an accident, not an attacker"), so this is the intended fail-open and not a defect.

claim: the `shep.toml` read error (`.ok()`) and parse error (`is_ok_and`) are both discarded, so `allow_read` silently becomes false and the reveal gate is closed with no explanation
reason: Treating a missing or unparseable `shep.toml` as `false` is a documented, deliberate fail-closed default (secrets.rs:71-73), but both errors are dropped, so the pane chrome still says `[secrets] allow_read = false in shep.toml` (pane_chrome.rs:33) when the file sets `true` and simply fails to read or parse, and the operator gets no hint why.

claim: a `secrets::get` error is turned into `None` by `.ok().flatten()`, so an unreadable store looks identical to a slot that was removed
reason: The doc comment on `stored_value` (secrets.rs:161) says `None` covers an unreadable store as well as a slot that has gone, and the caller in ui_event_loop.rs:359-363 treats a join failure the same way; this is a documented design choice, and the model's separate `unreadable` field already reports a store that will not read.

claim: `copy_to_clipboard`'s `io::Result` is discarded, so a failed stdout write is never reported; the pane still says the copy was sent
reason: The discard at crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/ui_event_loop.rs:509 is intentional and documented in the comment above it: a broken stdout pipe leaves nothing useful to do, and the pane's wording already says 'sent', not 'arrived'.

claim: `handle.await.ok().flatten()` drops both a panicked reveal task and a store error into "no value", so the failure is invisible to the operator
reason: Line 363 only flattens `Option<Option<String>>`, and dropping the join error there is a documented, deliberate choice; the store error is really discarded earlier at `crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/secrets.rs:174` (`secrets::get(...).ok().flatten()`), so a store error does show up as 'no value' but the finding blames the wrong line and its panic half is intended.

claim: a dog section that fails to parse as TOML becomes an empty value map (`.ok()`/`unwrap_or_default()`), so the pane shows schema defaults as if the operator had configured nothing
reason: The section text comes from the daemon's `dog_section` (crates/shep-daemon/src/dogs/config.rs:31), which only returns it after `DogsConfig::load` has parsed the whole `dogs.toml`, and it re-roots the section as valid TOML, so the `.ok()`/`unwrap_or_default()` fallback at config.rs:157 can't be reached with a section that fails to parse.

claim: `requests.try_send(Sent::Lambs{..})` on a full channel is dropped (also `polls.try_send(())` at `ui_event_loop.rs:232`), and a dropped repair poll is never retried
reason: A dropped poll is harmless because a full poll channel (capacity 8 at entry.rs:110) already holds a queued `()`, and the link task runs a `reconcile` for it (link.rs:175); a dropped `Sent::Lambs` shows only as "not read yet" and is sent again on the next `Effect::RefreshSelected`, which snapshots also raise (entry.rs:366-373), so nothing is lost for good.

claim: `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` drops the draw error and still clears `dirty`, so a dead terminal shows a frozen screen with no error.
reason: At line 167, `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` throws away the io::Error, then sets `dirty = false` and records `last_draw` as if the draw worked, so a draw failure is never shown or logged, the loop keeps running and the screen stays frozen.

claim: `Some(Err(_)) | None` drops the key-source error and retires the keyboard arm, so the UI stays up and ignores every key.
reason: The behavior is real and deliberate: the comment at ui_event_loop.rs:187-190 treats a key-source error as permanent and retires the arm to avoid a spin, but in raw mode that leaves only SIGTERM able to quit, and whether crossterm's `EventStream` errors are truly permanent (not, say, a transient EINTR) is not settled by this code.

claim: `notes` (per-stream read errors) is only surfaced when no lines were read, so an unreadable stderr log is hidden whenever stdout has lines.
reason: In `read` (`tail.rs:137`), per-stream errors pushed to `notes` only reach `tail.note` inside `if tail.lines.is_empty()`, so if stdout yields lines and stderr fails with a permission error or is missing, that error is silently dropped.

claim: `read_to_string(daemon_config).ok()` discards the shep.toml read error, so reveal is silently disabled (`allow_read` false).
reason: Treating an unreadable shep.toml as absent fails closed: `allow_read` stays false, which is the safe default for a secret-reveal gate. A missing file is the normal case, and a parse error is handled the same way through `is_ok_and`, so this is deliberate conservative behaviour rather than a bug.

claim: `secrets::get(..).ok().flatten()` discards the store read error on reveal.
reason: The doc comment on `stored_value` says it returns `None` "when the store will not read", so `.ok().flatten()` implements the documented contract rather than accidentally dropping an error.

claim: `handle.await.ok().flatten()` turns a panicked reveal task, an unreadable store and a vanished slot into the same silent "no value".
reason: At ui_event_loop.rs:363, `.ok().flatten()` turns a panicked task and a vanished slot into the same None, and `stored_value` (secrets.rs:174) already turns an unreadable store into None with `secrets::get(...).ok().flatten()`, so an I/O or parse error looks exactly like a missing value; the comment covers only the panic case and never mentions the store error being dropped.

claim: `Terminate::install().ok()` discards the install error, so the SIGTERM arm never fires and nothing says why.
reason: Every other call site (`dog/bark/event_loop.rs:44`, `dog/metrics/mod.rs:181`, `serve/worker.rs:101`) matches on the install error. The lookout alone turns it into `None` with `.ok()`. If registration fails, SIGTERM keeps its default action and kills the process without restoring the terminal, and nothing reports why.

claim: `let _ = copy_to_clipboard(..)` ignores the stdout write error while the pane says the value was sent.
reason: The ignore is deliberate and documented at ui_event_loop.rs:504-507: a failed stdout write means a broken pipe, which leaves the TUI nothing useful to do, and the pane only claims the value was sent, not that it arrived.

claim: `Regex::new(pattern).ok()?` treats an uncompilable schema pattern as no constraint, so every value is accepted.
reason: Failing open on a pattern that won't compile is deliberate: the doc comment on `refusal` (validation.rs:221-224) says so, reasoning that if a dog ships a broken regex, the operator shouldn't be locked out of that setting.

claim: `resolve_control` maps a `kv::get` error to `Control::Allowed`, so an unreadable kv.json fails open and the error is never reported.
reason: The fail-open is deliberate and documented in the doc comment at `crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/entry.rs:147-153` ("unreadable it leaves control on: the gate stops an accident, not an attacker"), so the behaviour matches the intended design; silently ignoring the error is the only real gap, and at most it's a diagnostics nit.

claim: `let _ = msgs.send(Msg::Retrying { .. })` ignores a closed UI channel, so the ladder keeps redialling until its attempts run out.
reason: The `Retrying` send result at link.rs:116 is discarded, so once the UI receiver closes the ladder keeps sleeping and redialling until it has used up `RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS`; this breaks the doc contract that it 'ends … when the UI stops listening', although in production the harm is small because entry.rs:143 calls `link.abort()` after the UI exits.

claim: a `None` reveal value clears `pending_reveal` and returns without a notice, so the keypress looks unbound.
reason: `reveal_secret` in secrets.rs returns `None` when the stored slot has disappeared since the model was built, and `on_revealed` (reveal_secret.rs:126) then clears `pending_reveal` and returns without setting `self.notice`, so pressing `v` shows no value and no message, unlike the refusal and copy paths, which both set a notice.

claim: `Err(_other) => Ok(())` swallows every request error except `Closed`, so a failed `ListFlock` leaves the snapshot stale and unreported.
reason: The swallow is deliberate and documented in the doc comment on `reconcile` (link.rs:210-213): one failed poll must not take the connection down, and a dead connection still climbs the ladder because its subscription ends; the only real flaw is that the `Closed` and `_other` arms are redundant, not a correctness bug.

claim: `LevelMatcher::compile(rules).ok()` discards the compile error and falls back to the default classifier (the comment calls this unreachable).
reason: The `.ok()` fallback is intentional and documented: `normalize` in `crates/shep-core/src/config/normalize/resolved_app.rs:291` already compiles the same rules with `LevelMatcher::compile` and rejects any that fail, so an invalid list can't be stored and this branch is unreachable, with the fallback kept as a safer default.

claim: the parse → `to_value` → `as_object` chain ends in `unwrap_or_default()`, so a dogs.toml section that does not parse gives an empty values map with no notice.
reason: The section comes from the daemon's `dog_section` (crates/shep-daemon/src/dogs/config.rs:31). It parses `dogs.toml` first and returns `DogError::Config` if the file is broken, then sends back a re-rooted TOML table. Any string that reaches `dog()` therefore always parses as `toml::Table`, and turns into a JSON object when converted, so the silent `unwrap_or_default()` branch can't be hit in practice.

claim: `parse().unwrap_or(1)` hides a parse failure of the instance count (the comment says it cannot fail for a sheep).
reason: The comment documents why the parse can't fail: `instances` is a plain `u32` on every sheep's `AppConfig`, and `close_offer` refuses dogs before building the dialog, so `unwrap_or(1)` is an unreachable fallback, not a hidden failure.

claim: `edited_section_with` returns `None` for an unrepresentable number as well as for a parse failure, so the caller gives the wrong reason.
reason: `arbitrary_precision` is not enabled on serde_json anywhere in the workspace, and without it `Number::as_f64` always returns `Some` (a u64 above i64::MAX becomes a float), so the `(None, None)` arm at `crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/pane/edit.rs:107` can't be reached and the unrepresentable-number case never produces the misleading "does not parse" notice.

claim: `serde_json::to_value(config).ok()` gives an empty values map if serialising `AppConfig` fails (practically infallible).
reason: Serialising a plain derived-Serialize `AppConfig` into `serde_json::Value` can't realistically fail, and this is a display-only pane, so the empty-map fallback is a harmless defensive default rather than a defect.

claim: `handle.await.ok().flatten()` folds a `JoinError` from the reveal task to `None`, while the sibling `LoadDogPane` arm (`:433`) surfaces the same panic, so the two arms disagree.
reason: The difference is on purpose and the code says so: the comment at :359-362 explains that a failed reveal shows no value because the operator can't act on a notice about a panic, while the LoadDogPane comment at :427-430 explains that its failure is reported so the keystroke doesn't look unbound, so this isn't an accidental inconsistency.

claim: `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` discards the draw error, then sets `dirty = false` and `last_draw`, so a persistent backend failure freezes the display and the loop keeps running.
reason: At `ui_event_loop.rs:167`, `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` drops the error and then clears `dirty` and sets `last_draw` anyway, so a backend that keeps failing leaves the screen frozen while the loop runs on with no exit or report, even though the same loop does retire its key and link arms when they fail permanently.

claim: `Some(Err(_)) | None => keys_done = true` drops the crossterm read error and retires the keyboard arm for good, so `q` no longer quits, the screen looks alive, and only SIGTERM ends it.
reason: Retiring the arm is a deliberate, commented design choice: a crossterm EventStream error or end means the tty input is gone for good, so `q` could not arrive anyway, and retiring the arm is what stops it spinning above the link and heartbeat arms; the only small point that holds is that the error is not logged.

claim: a `None` value returns with no `Notice`, so a failed reveal (unreadable store or panicked task) just clears `pending_reveal` and the keypress shows nothing.
reason: The silence is on purpose: the comment at `crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/ui_event_loop.rs:359-362` says a failed read or a panicked task counts as "no value", and that a notice was left out because it would name a panic the operator can't act on; `Msg::Revealed` also documents `None` as "slot no longer resolves or store would not read".

claim: `environment().unwrap_or_default()` turns a missing tab into `""` and sends a `WriteSecret` for environment `""` instead of refusing.
reason: The `""` fallback can't be reached: `secrets.rs:107` always adds `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS`, so `environments` is never empty, and `tab` is clamped to `len-1` on model refresh (`update.rs:537`) and on tab keys (`secrets_keys.rs:62-65`), so `environment()` always returns `Some`.

claim: `secrets::get(..).ok().flatten()` discards the store's read error, so an unreadable store looks the same as a slot that has gone.
reason: The doc comment on `stored_value` (secrets.rs:161-162) says it returns `None` both when the store will not read and when the slot has gone, and the only caller, `on_revealed`, treats both cases the same by drawing nothing, so this is the intended contract rather than a defect.

claim: `regex::Regex::new(pattern).ok()?` discards the compile error for a dog-published `pattern`, so a bad pattern disables validation and every typed value is accepted.
reason: The fail-open is deliberate: the doc comment at validation.rs:221 says the lookout 'Fails open on a `pattern` that does not compile', and the test `a_pattern_that_does_not_compile_refuses_nothing` (line 720) pins that behaviour, so this is the intended design rather than a defect.

claim: `confirm_secret_delete` has already consumed `armed` and then returns `Effect::None` with no notice when `environment()` is `None`, so Enter on a confirmed delete silently does nothing.
reason: `arm_secret_delete` never requires `environment()` to be `Some`: its all-slot check uses `is_some_and`, which just skips when there is no environment. So a delete can be armed with no environment, and then `confirm_secret_delete` takes `armed` and returns `Effect::None` without setting a notice. I did not check whether the model can actually hold rows with an empty `environments` list, which is what would make this reachable in practice.

claim: `serde_json::to_value(config).ok()…unwrap_or_default()` yields an empty value map on a serialize failure, so the sheep pane shows every field as default with no error.
reason: The code does silently fall back to an empty map, but serializing a derived-`Serialize` config struct to a `serde_json::Value` cannot fail in practice. It can only fail on non-string map keys or a custom serializer error, so the reported failure is theoretical rather than a reachable bug.

claim: `_ => LambWalk::Failed` drops the `RequestError` (RPC message versus transport), so the panel cannot say why a lamb read failed.
reason: The catch-all at lambs.rs:24 turns every `RequestError` (an RPC error reply or a closed transport), an unrecognised reply, and a missing sheep (line 19) into a bare `LambWalk::Failed`, so `detail.rs:276` shows the same 'the shepherd did not answer that request' for all of them, which is wrong whenever the shepherd did answer with an error.

claim: `read_to_string(..).ok()` plus `is_ok_and(..)` discards both the `shep.toml` read and parse errors, so a broken config reads as `allow_read = false` with no reason shown (the fail-closed default is documented).
reason: At lines 143-145, both the `shep.toml` read error (`.ok()`) and the `DaemonConfig::load` parse error (`.is_ok_and`) are discarded, so a broken config turns into `allow_read = false`, and `SecretsModel` has no field to tell the operator why, while unreadable stores do get one (`unreadable`); failing closed is deliberate, but the silence is a real gap.

claim: `let _ = copy_to_clipboard(..)` discards the stdout write error, so a failed copy is indistinguishable from a sent one.
reason: The discard is deliberate and documented in the comment above it (a broken stdout pipe leaves the TUI nothing useful to do, and the pane only claims the value was sent), and even a successful OSC 52 write can't confirm the terminal set the clipboard.

claim: `_unrecognised => Ok(Vec::new())` turns an unrecognised `ListFlock` reply into a successful empty flock, which would blank the table rather than signal a failed poll.
reason: Daemon errors come back as `RequestError::Rpc` and never reach this match, but any other non-`Flock` success reply (a newer daemon's `#[non_exhaustive]` variant, or a misrouted reply) becomes `Ok(Vec::new())`, so the lookout shows an empty flock instead of a failed poll; this is unlikely in practice, so severity is low.

claim: `Terminate::install().ok()` discards the signal-handler install error, so SIGTERM handling is silently off and the SIGTERM arm never fires.
reason: `Terminate::install()` only fails if the OS refuses to register the handler, which almost never happens on a normal tokio runtime, so `.ok()` just degrades to no SIGTERM arm in that rare case; SIGTERM handling is not silently off in normal operation, even though the discard is undocumented.

claim: `LevelMatcher::compile(rules).ok()` discards the compile error and falls back to the default classifier (low: the doc argues `normalize()` makes it unreachable).
reason: The fallback is deliberate and documented: `normalize()` rejects rules that fail to compile before they can be stored, and falling back to `level_of` is the stated choice over a feed that classifies nothing, so discarding the error loses nothing actionable.

claim: `parse().unwrap_or(1)` hides a parse failure and would understate the reload row's process count (low: the comment argues it is unreachable).
reason: For a sheep, `pane.value("instances")` renders a stored `u32` from the serialized `AppConfig` as JSON, so parsing it back cannot fail, and `close_offer` rejects a dog before this constructor runs, so the `unwrap_or(1)` fallback is never reached.

claim: `reconcile` maps `Err(_other) => Ok(())`, so a failed `ListFlock` after a bus lag (timeout, RPC error) is dropped and the flock table stays stale until the next poll.
reason: Dropping the failed poll is deliberate and documented in the doc comment at link.rs:210-213: one bad round trip must not tear down the connection, and the next periodic poll repairs the table, which the finding itself acknowledges.

claim: `resolve_control` matches `_ => Control::Allowed`, so a `kv::get` error (corrupt `kv.json`, permission denied) silently turns off the `lookout.allow_control false` read-only gate.
reason: The doc comment at crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/entry.rs:147-153 states on purpose that an unreadable kv.json leaves control on, because the gate is there to stop an accident, not an attacker, so failing open is the documented behaviour and not a bug.

claim: `Some(Err(_)) | None` retires the key arm for good on any key-source read error with no notice, so the dashboard cannot be quit from the keyboard.
reason: The code does this on purpose to avoid a busy loop, but once `keys_done` is set with raw mode on, Ctrl-C and `q` never arrive and only SIGTERM can end the loop, so after a key-source error the dashboard stays up with no way to quit from the keyboard and no message, when breaking out with an error would have exited cleanly.

claim: `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` drops the draw error and still stamps `last_draw`, so a dead stdout leaves the loop spinning with no display and no exit.
reason: The draw error is dropped, but the loop does not spin: every iteration blocks in `tokio::select!` on signals, keys, messages and the heartbeat, and the quit key and SIGTERM still end it, so a dead stdout costs only the display.

claim: `let _ = msgs.send(Msg::Retrying { attempt }).await;` discards the send failure, so after the UI has gone the ladder keeps sleeping and re-dialing (up to about 7.75s) instead of returning.
reason: At crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/link.rs:116 the result of `send(Msg::Retrying)` is thrown away, so once the receiver is dropped the loop keeps sleeping and re-dialing until it runs out of attempts. This contradicts the doc comment's "or when the UI stops listening", and the `Relinked` send and `run_connected` both return on `UiGone`.

claim: `Terminate::install().ok()` drops the handler-registration error, so a SIGTERM then kills the process past `RestoreGuard` and leaves the terminal in raw mode.
reason: If `tokio::signal::unix::signal(SIGTERM)` fails to register, `.ok()` turns the error into `None`, so SIGTERM keeps its default action and kills the process without unwinding. `RestoreGuard` never runs and the terminal stays in raw mode. Registration almost never fails, but nothing reports or handles it when it does.

claim: `_unrecognised => Ok(Vec::new())` turns an unknown `ListFlock` reply into an empty flock, so every sheep vanishes from the table until the next poll.
reason: `reconcile` in `link.rs:217` sends any `Ok(rows)` straight to the table as a `Msg::Snapshot`, so an unrecognised reply (for example an error `Response`) empties the table until the next poll, whereas an `Err` is dropped and the last good snapshot stays on screen.

claim: `regex::Regex::new(pattern).ok()?` skips validation without a word when a dog's published `pattern` does not compile, so every value is accepted for that field.
reason: Failing open on a pattern that doesn't compile is deliberate: the doc comment at validation.rs:221 says so, and the test `a_pattern_that_does_not_compile_refuses_nothing` checks that exact behavior.

claim: `read_to_string(..).ok()` plus `DaemonConfig::load(..).is_ok_and(..)` silently closes the `allow_read` reveal gate on any unreadable or malformed `shep.toml`, with no cause shown.
reason: Failing closed is the right call, but when `shep.toml` is malformed or unreadable the load error is thrown away and the pane chrome (`view/secrets/pane_chrome.rs:33`) prints `allow_read = false in shep.toml`, which misleads an operator who has set it to true.

claim: `secrets::get(..).ok().flatten()` turns a store read error into "no value", so a failed reveal looks the same as a slot that has gone.
reason: This is deliberate. The doc comment on `stored_value` (secrets.rs:161-163) says `None` covers a store that will not read as well as a slot that has gone, and the caller in `ui_event_loop.rs` treats a join failure the same way on purpose, so in every case the reveal just shows nothing.

claim: `_ => LambWalk::Failed` drops the `RequestError` for a failed lamb fetch, so the cause is never recorded or shown.
reason: At `lambs.rs:24` the wildcard arm maps an `Err(RequestError)` to `LambWalk::Failed`, and that variant holds no data, so the cause is lost; the config and dog panes (`config_pane.rs:77-83`, `dog_pane.rs:67-73`) match `Err(RequestError::Rpc(err))` and `Err(other)` to keep it, although the comment at lines 22-23 suggests this pane drops it on purpose.

claim: `ConfigPane::dog` turns a `toml::Table` parse or JSON conversion failure into an empty map, so a dog whose section does not parse opens as unset fields with no notice until close.
reason: The daemon's `dog_section` (crates/shep-daemon/src/dogs/config.rs:31) only returns a section after `DogsConfig::load` and `toml_edit` have both parsed the whole file, and it returns an error on a bad `dogs.toml`, so the section the pane receives is already valid TOML and the `unwrap_or_default` fallback can't be reached in practice.

claim: `LevelMatcher::compile(rules).ok()` discards the compile error and silently falls back to the built-in classifier.
reason: The fallback is deliberate and documented at level.rs:80-83: `shep_core::config::normalize()` rejects rule lists that won't compile before they can be stored, so this branch can't be reached, and falling back is safer than a feed that classifies nothing.

claim: `serde_json::to_value(config).ok()…unwrap_or_default()` turns a serialization failure into an empty value map, so every field draws as unset.
reason: `config` is a derived-`Serialize` `AppConfig` with string-keyed maps, so `serde_json::to_value` can't realistically fail and it always serializes to an object; the empty-map fallback never runs, and the pattern matches the defensive `unwrap_or_default` the same function uses for the schema lookups.

claim: `handle.await.ok().flatten()` folds a panicked `spawn_blocking` reveal into "no value"; the comment says this is deliberate, but the panic is never surfaced.
reason: The swallow is a documented, reasoned design choice (a panic in a UI reveal has nothing actionable to show the operator, and the result renders the same as a missing slot), so it is intentional, not a defect.

claim: `let _ = requests.try_send(Sent::Lambs { id })` drops a lamb fetch when the channel is full or closed, and the pane shows "not read yet" rather than the cause.
reason: The drop is deliberate and documented at ui_event_loop.rs:124-127 and app/update.rs:274: a full channel means a request is already queued and the next `lambs_dirty` pass fetches again, so "not read yet" is the intended transient state, not a hidden error.

claim: low: `drifted_fields` maps a failed `serde_json::to_value` on either config to `Vec::new()`, so a serialization failure looks like "no drift" and nothing is logged or returned.
reason: The fallback is deliberate and documented in the comment ('An empty result means no drift, or none could be computed'), and `serde_json::to_value` on a derived-`Serialize` `AppConfig` has no realistic failure path, so this is not a defect worth acting on.

claim: `let _ = msgs.send(Msg::Frozen { .. }).await;` discards the send result; benign, since the task returns next anyway.
reason: A send error only means the receiver (the UI loop) has been dropped, so nobody is left to show the freeze, and the task returns on the next line either way; discarding the result is correct, not a defect.

claim: low: `holds_token` discards the `Completion` from `walk` (`let _ =`), so an unclosed `{{` makes `holds_secret` and `holds_shep_home` return false instead of signalling.
reason: The `holds_*` functions are boolean predicates, and the doc comment defines them as matching what the renderers would substitute. An unclosed `{{` holds no token, so `false` is the correct answer, and `validate` (template.rs:335) already reports the malformed value as `TemplateError::Unclosed`.

claim: low: `.map_err(|_| ...)` drops the `UpDuration` parse error, so a bad `SHEP_MAX_CRON_SLEEP` is reported as an invalid value without saying whether the unit, number or format was wrong. The error is still surfaced, so this is the weakest finding.
reason: Line 143 discards the `UpDuration` parse error with `map_err(|_| ...)`, so `BadEnvValue("SHEP_MAX_CRON_SLEEP", v)` reports the key and raw value but not why parsing failed; the variable is still refused, which keeps this low severity and matches how `SHEP_LOG_LEVEL` is handled above it.

claim: low: `render_positional` discards the `Completion` from `walk` (`let _: Result<Completion, Infallible>`), so an unclosed `{{` silently truncates the rendered value. It depends on callers running `validate` first, and nothing enforces that.
reason: `render_positional` is a public, infallible fn that drops `walk`'s `Completion`. Its only guard against truncating at an unclosed `{{` is a doc comment saying to call `validate` first, and no type enforces that. The in-tree callers go through normalize, which does validate, so the risk sits in the public API and the finding is correctly rated low.

claim: `drifted_fields` drops a `serde_json::to_value` failure in the `let-else` and returns an empty list, so two differing configs report "no drift"; the doc comment admits this, and a failure is unlikely.
reason: The let-else at behavior.rs:114 does return an empty Vec when either `serde_json::to_value` call fails, even though `self != other` was already established. The comment admits this, so the finding is accurate, but it is low severity because serializing an `AppConfig` is effectively infallible.

claim: low: `std::env::var(key).ok()` turns a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` into "unset". `shep_home` then falls back to another directory or `None`, and `{{SHEP_HOME}}` templates fail with the misleading `NoShepHome` error.
reason: `normalize` (resolved_app.rs:62) passes `std::env::var(key).ok()` into `paths::shep_home`, and that turns `Err(NotUnicode)` into `None`, the same value as an unset variable. So a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` silently falls back to `<home>/.shep`, or with no home directory `{{SHEP_HOME}}` fails with `NoShepHome`. That error says no shep home was found, when the real problem is that `SHEP_HOME` isn't UTF-8.

claim: `.map_err(|_| ...)` discards the `UpDuration` parse cause, so the operator sees the bad `SHEP_MAX_CRON_SLEEP` value but not whether the unit or the number was wrong; the error is still returned, not swallowed.
reason: At config.rs:143, `.map_err(|_| ...)` really does drop the `UpDuration` parse error, and `BadEnvValue(&str, String)` has no field to carry a source, so the operator only sees the raw value; the impact is low, though, because the sibling env keys handle bad values the same way and the error is still returned.

claim: silent-discard: `drifted_fields` returns an empty Vec, which reads as "no drift", when either `serde_json::to_value` call fails, so a caller can't tell a serialization failure from real equality.
reason: The code comment says outright that an empty result means "no drift, or none could be computed", and `serde_json::to_value` on a derived-Serialize config with string-keyed maps cannot realistically fail, so the fallback is intended and harmless rather than a hidden error.

claim: silent-discard: `Path::is_file()` turns any stat error (such as permission denied) into `false`, so an unreadable Flockfile is skipped with no error and discovery moves on or returns `None`.
reason: A Flockfile you can't read still passes `stat`, because `stat` only needs search permission on the directory, so `is_file()` returns true and the later read fails loudly; `is_file()` only returns false when the whole directory can't be searched, and then every candidate fails the same way, not one unreadable file being skipped for the next.

claim: `std::env::var(key).ok()` turns `VarError::NotUnicode` into `None`, so a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` is silently ignored and `{{SHEP_HOME}}` expands against the fallback home.
reason: At line 62, `normalize` reads `SHEP_HOME` with `std::env::var(key).ok()`, so a non-UTF-8 value becomes `None` and `shep_home` falls back to `<home>/.shep`, while the CLI's own home resolution (`crates/shep-cli/src/home.rs:67`) uses `var_os` and honours that same value, so `{{SHEP_HOME}}` points at a different directory from the one shep actually uses.

claim: silent-discard: `std::env::var(key).ok()` turns a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` (`VarError::NotUnicode`) into "unset", so the override is ignored and the default home is used.
reason: `normalize` passes `|key| std::env::var(key).ok()` into `paths::shep_home`. If `SHEP_HOME` is set to a non-UTF-8 path, that returns `None`, so `home_under` quietly falls back to the default home and `{{SHEP_HOME}}` renders the wrong directory, with no error.

claim: silent-discard (weak): `.map_err(|_| ..)` drops the `UpDuration` parse error's cause for `SHEP_MAX_CRON_SLEEP`, so the operator sees only the raw value and not why it failed to parse.
reason: The closure `.map_err(|_| DaemonConfigError::BadEnvValue("SHEP_MAX_CRON_SLEEP", v))` at config.rs:143 does discard the `UpDuration` parse error. `BadEnvValue` has no field to carry a cause, so the operator sees only the raw value. The impact is small because the other `BadEnvValue` users (`SHEP_LOG_JSON`, `SHEP_LOG_LEVEL`) parse to an `Option` and never have a cause to lose.

claim: `p.is_file()` turns any I/O error, such as permission denied on a `Flockfile.toml`, into "not there". `discover` then skips it and can return a lower-priority file, or `None`, with no error.
reason: `is_file()` only needs `stat`, which works on a file with no read permission, so an unreadable `Flockfile.toml` is still found and the error shows up when it is read; the remaining silent cases are a dangling or looping symlink, which skips to a lower-priority name, and a directory without search permission, which returns `None`, and neither is the permission-denied-on-the-file case the finding describes.

claim: carried: `drifted_fields` drops a `serde_json::to_value` failure in its let-else and returns an empty `Vec`, so "could not compare" reads as "no drift".
reason: The swallow is deliberate and commented at behavior.rs:113 ("An empty result means no drift, or none could be computed"), and the function returns early when `self == other`, so the fallback only runs for configs that really differ; `serde_json::to_value` on a derived-`Serialize` struct with string keys has no practical failure path, which makes this a theoretical gap rather than a reachable bug.

claim: carried: `p.is_file()` turns any metadata I/O error into `false`, so `discover` silently skips an unreadable higher-priority Flockfile and picks a lower-priority one or returns `None`.
reason: `is_file()` uses `stat`, and `stat` succeeds on a file whose contents are unreadable, so such a Flockfile is still found and its read error surfaces later; the errors that do make `stat` fail (no search permission on the directory, a broken symlink or loop) either hit every candidate equally or mean the file isn't there.

claim: `.unwrap_or_default()` turns a missing or non-array `app` value into an empty table list. Every app then gets an empty `declared` and `declared_env` set with no error, so all fields count as undeclared. The comment above it argues this can't happen, but nothing enforces that.
reason: `parse_nonempty_apps` runs first and deserializes into `RawFlockfile`, where `app` is a plain `Vec` with no alias and with `deny_unknown_fields`, and it refuses an empty list; so any document that reaches line 64 has `app` as a non-empty array and the `unwrap_or_default()` never fires.

claim: `std::env::var(key).ok()` drops `VarError::NotUnicode`, so a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` is treated as unset and `{{SHEP_HOME}}` silently resolves under `~/.shep` instead of failing.
reason: `normalize` passes `std::env::var(key).ok()` into `paths::shep_home`, so a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` becomes `None` and `{{SHEP_HOME}}` resolves to `<home>/.shep` without an error; the CLI's `require_utf8` refuses that value earlier (`crates/shep-cli/src/home.rs:82`), but `normalize` is a public shep-core function and other callers (library users, or the daemon started without the CLI) get the silent fallback.

claim: `std::env::var(key).ok()` drops `VarError::NotUnicode`, so a non-UTF-8 `$SHEP_HOME` reads as unset and `normalize` silently falls back to `<home>/.shep` (or to no shep home at all if there is no home dir).
reason: `normalize` reads `$SHEP_HOME` with `std::env::var(key).ok()`, so a non-UTF-8 value turns into `None` and `paths::shep_home` falls back to `<home>/.shep` (or to `None` when there is no home directory), while the CLI's `resolve_paths_in` (`crates/shep-cli/src/home.rs:76`) calls `require_utf8` and refuses the same value, so `{{SHEP_HOME}}` quietly renders to a different directory instead of failing.

claim: `std::env::var(key).ok()` drops `VarError::NotUnicode`, so a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` is treated as unset and `normalize` silently resolves against `~/.shep` instead of failing.
reason: `normalize` at resolved_app.rs:62 reads `SHEP_HOME` with `std::env::var(key).ok()`, so a non-UTF-8 value turns into `None` and `paths::shep_home` falls back to `~/.shep`; the CLI's `home.rs` refuses a non-UTF-8 home loudly through `require_utf8`, but this public shep-core entry point has no such check and quietly resolves against the wrong root.

claim: `joined.to_string_lossy().into_owned()` does the same to an expanded `~/` path, and `expand_home_tilde` is public and returns `Ok`.
reason: `value` is already UTF-8, but a non-UTF-8 `home` is silently converted to U+FFFD by `to_string_lossy()`, so the public `expand_home_tilde` returns `Ok` with a path that points somewhere else instead of returning an error.

claim: `home.to_string_lossy()` on the `SHEP_HOME` path silently replaces non-UTF-8 bytes with U+FFFD, so a child gets a path that names a different directory.
reason: `crates/shep-core/src/paths.rs:236-249` documents that `SHEP_HOME` is taken as a `String` on purpose: the CLI refuses a non-UTF-8 home at its only entry point, and a library caller has already produced a `String`, so `to_string_lossy()` at `template.rs:360` never has non-UTF-8 bytes to replace.

claim: `render` discards the `Completion::Unclosed` returned by `walk`, so `abc{{name` renders as `abc` with the tail silently truncated; the function is public and relies on callers having run `validate`.
reason: `render` does throw away `walk`'s `Completion`, so `abc{{name` really does come out as `abc`; the docstring admits this and puts the burden on callers to run `validate` first, and the only callers (`crates/shep-daemon/src/assemble/spawn_spec.rs`) get values that went through normalize's `validate`, so it is a real footgun in a public API but nothing currently reachable triggers it.

claim: `render_positional` also discards `Completion::Unclosed` (`let _: Result<Completion, Infallible>`), so an unclosed `{{` truncates the value silently; `normalize` validates first, but the function is `pub`.
reason: The truncation is intended and documented: the doc comment at template.rs:378-379 says "Call `validate` first: an unclosed `{{` renders truncated at that point," and `render` states the same precondition, so this is a documented contract rather than a silent defect.

claim: `kahn` does `break` when no node is ready, so a stall (the comment calls it impossible) drops the remaining nodes from `stages` with no `debug_assert!` and no record in `BootPlan`.
reason: The stall can't happen: a node is only held back by a dependency still in `left`, which would need a cycle inside `ordered`, and cycles plus anything depending on them are lifted out before `kahn` runs. So the `break` is a defensive arm that can't be reached, and no nodes are dropped; adding a `debug_assert!` would be a hygiene tweak, not a bug fix.

claim: carried: `map_err(|_| ...)` throws away `UpDuration`'s parse reason; it still surfaces as `BadEnvValue`, so only the reason is lost (low).
reason: Line 143 uses `map_err(|_| DaemonConfigError::BadEnvValue("SHEP_MAX_CRON_SLEEP", v))`, which drops the `UpDuration` parse error: the operator sees the key and the bad value but not why it failed. That matches the low-severity finding.

claim: `std::env::var(key).ok()` drops `NotUnicode`, so a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` reads as unset and `shep_home` falls back to `<home>/.shep`; `{{SHEP_HOME}}` then expands to a different directory with no error.
reason: `normalize` is a public shep-core function, and its `std::env::var(key).ok()` turns a `NotUnicode` `SHEP_HOME` into `None`, so `shep_home` silently falls back to `<home>/.shep` with no error; the CLI refuses a non-UTF-8 home earlier through `require_utf8` in `resolve_paths_in` (crates/shep-cli/src/home.rs), but any other caller of `normalize` gets `{{SHEP_HOME}}` expanded to the wrong directory.

claim: `drifted_fields` returns an empty Vec, meaning "no drift", when `serde_json::to_value` fails on either config. The `Err` is discarded, so two configs that differ are reported as identical.
reason: The empty result on a serialization failure is deliberate and stated in the comment and doc at behavior.rs:110-113 ('no drift, or none could be computed'), and `serde_json::to_value` on a derived-Serialize `AppConfig` has no practical way to fail, so the case the finding describes is documented and effectively unreachable.

claim: `p.is_file()` turns any stat error (for example EACCES on `Flockfile.toml`) into `false`, so discovery silently falls through to a lower-priority name such as `flockfile.json` and loads the wrong file.
reason: `stat` needs search permission on the directory, not read permission on the file, and every candidate sits in the same `dir`, so EACCES would hit all ten names equally and nothing lower-priority could be loaded instead; the only remaining trigger is a looping or dangling `Flockfile.toml` symlink, where falling through to the next name is defensible behaviour.

claim: `as_str().unwrap_or_default()` on `init.group` means a field with no group silently sorts last; only the `every_field_carries_a_group_and_a_blurb` test catches it.
reason: The fallback is deliberate: the schema is compile-time data, and `every_field_carries_a_group_and_a_blurb` (scaffold.rs:605) fails CI on a missing group and on a group outside GROUP_ORDER, so no field can sort last silently.

claim: a field with no `init.example` silently falls back to `String::new()`, so the scaffold would emit an empty-string value with no error, and in JSON that line is live.
reason: `literal` falls back to `String::new()` when `init.example` is missing, unlike `blurb`, which panics, and no test requires every field to carry an example; a field with no example and no default would print `""` in the live JSON scaffold. The JSON test only checks that `name` and `script` are non-empty, so the bug is latent: I did not confirm that any current field triggers it.

claim: `to_string_lossy()` silently replaces non-UTF-8 bytes in the home path with U+FFFD. The expanded `script`, `cwd` and log paths then point at a directory that does not exist, with no error.
reason: `expand_home_tilde` sends a non-UTF-8 `home` through `to_string_lossy()`, which swaps the bad bytes for U+FFFD and returns `Ok`, and `expand_paths` writes that corrupted path into `script`, `cwd`, `out_file` and `err_file` without any error (there is no `TildeError` variant for a non-UTF-8 home).

claim: `render` discards the `Completion` from `walk(..)?`. An unclosed `{{` returns `Completion::Unclosed`, so the value is silently truncated and the text after the `{{` is dropped, with no error from a public function. The doc says "call validate first" and nothing enforces it.
reason: The truncation is documented behaviour, not a silent defect: `render`'s doc comment (template.rs:408-410) says it assumes `validate` already passed and that "an unclosed `{{` renders truncated at that point", and `validate` turns `Completion::Unclosed` into `TemplateError::Unclosed` (template.rs:335), so this is an intentional precondition split rather than a lost error; I did not check that every caller runs `validate` first.

claim: `.map_err(|_| BadEnvValue(..))` discards the `UpDuration` parse error. The operator sees "invalid value" with no reason (bad unit, overflow, and so on).
reason: At `config.rs:143` the `UpDuration` parse error is thrown away by `map_err(|_| ...)`, and `BadEnvValue` only holds the key name and the raw string, so the operator is never told why the value failed (bad unit, overflow, and so on).

claim: `path.starts_with("dog.")` also matches a top-level unknown key literally named `dog.x`, because serde_ignored renders a top-level map key with no prefix. That typo is silently swallowed instead of raising `UnknownKeys`.
reason: serde_ignored's Display for a Map/Struct path whose parent is Root writes only the key, so a quoted top-level key `"dog.x" = 1` (TOML) or `{"dog.x": 1}` (JSON) is reported as `dog.x`, matches `starts_with("dog.")`, and is dropped instead of raising `UnknownKeys`.

claim: `std::env::var(key).ok()` turns a set but non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` (`VarError::NotUnicode`) into `None`. `paths::shep_home` then falls back to `<home>/.shep`, so `{{SHEP_HOME}}` silently expands to the default home instead of the operator's.
reason: `normalize` reads `SHEP_HOME` through `std::env::var(key).ok()`, which turns `NotUnicode` into `None`. `paths::shep_home` then falls back to `<home>/.shep`, so `{{SHEP_HOME}}` expands to the default home without any error. The CLI's own resolver in `crates/shep-cli/src/home.rs` refuses a non-UTF-8 `--home`/`SHEP_HOME` with `require_utf8`, but `normalize` is a public shep-core function, so it can run without that check.

claim: `shep_home.map(|home| home.to_string_lossy())` silently corrupts a non-UTF-8 shep home in every rendered `{{SHEP_HOME}}` value handed to a child.
reason: The loss is a documented design choice: `paths.rs:236-249` explains that the CLI refuses a non-UTF-8 home at its entry point and that `resolve` takes a `String` lookup, so a non-UTF-8 home never reaches the `to_string_lossy` call at template.rs:360 to be corrupted.

claim: every backend error (TOML 43, YAML 50, JSON 54 and 57, JSON5 67 and 69) is flattened with `e.to_string()` into `FlockfileError::{Toml,Yaml,Json,Json5}(String)`. The typed error, its source chain and its span are lost.
reason: The flattening is true but intentional: `FlockfileError` (error.rs:14-17) derives `Clone`, `PartialEq` and `Eq` and documents each variant as 'carries its message', which keeps toml, saphyr, serde_json and json5 error types out of shep-core's public API; those types mostly can't be `Clone` or `Eq`, and their `to_string()` output already includes the line and column, so this is a deliberate design choice, not a defect.

claim: `toml::from_str(..).map_err(|e| Toml(e.to_string()))` flattens the parser error to a `String`. `DaemonConfigError` has no `source()`, so the chain and span are lost. Contrast `dogs.rs:45`, which keeps the error.
reason: `DaemonConfigError::Toml(String)` (daemon/error.rs:14) keeps only the parser's `to_string()`, and the empty `impl core::error::Error for DaemonConfigError {}` has no `source()`, so callers lose the typed `toml::de::Error` and its span; the rendered text survives in `Display`, while `DogsConfigError::Toml(toml::de::Error)` keeps the error and returns it from `source()`.

claim: `render_positional` discards `Result<Completion, Infallible>` with `let _:`. An unclosed `{{` truncates the output silently. The only in-crate caller, `normalize`, validates first. Low severity.
reason: The truncation on an unclosed `{{` is deliberate and documented: the doc comment on `render_positional` says "Call `validate` first: an unclosed `{{` renders truncated at that point", `render` carries the same contract, and the only caller validates first, so nothing is silently broken.

claim: when `kahn` stalls, `break` silently drops every unplaced node from the plan, so those sheep are never started. The comment argues it is unreachable, but nothing reports it.
reason: A stall in `kahn` needs a cycle among the nodes still in `left`, but Tarjan's `knots` lifts out every strongly connected component and self-loop, and `depends_on_a_cycle` holds out their dependents, so the input is acyclic and the `break` arm cannot be reached.

claim: `unwrap_or_else(|| String::new())` silently emits `""` for a field that has neither a real default nor an `init.example`. Uncommenting that line in a scaffold yields a wrongly typed value, and unlike `blurb` this case does not panic.
reason: `literal` (scaffold.rs:422-431) falls back to `""` whenever a field's schema default is null or empty and it has no `init.example`, and nothing checks that such fields carry an example: `init.example` appears nowhere else in scaffold.rs, and the only test named alongside it, `every_field_carries_a_group_and_a_blurb`, covers the blurb, not the example. So an `Option<u64>` or `Option<bool>` field without an example is scaffolded as `= ""` with no warning, whereas `blurb` would panic.

claim: `.map_err(|_| BadPort { target })` discards the `ParseIntError`, so empty, non-numeric and out-of-range ports all give the same message. Low severity.
reason: Empty ports never get here, because `parse_tcp` returns `MissingPort` for them first; non-numeric and out-of-range ports both get "has a port that is not a valid u16", which is accurate for both, so dropping the `ParseIntError` loses almost nothing.

claim: `parse_declared` uses `.unwrap_or_default()` when `app` is not an array or a table is not an object, so the declared key sets come back empty. That would read as "declared nothing", though the earlier typed parse makes it unreachable today. Low severity.
reason: The `.unwrap_or_default()` at file.rs:64 (and the `.flatten()` at :70) would quietly turn a shape mismatch into "declared nothing" rather than failing loudly. The typed `parse_nonempty_apps` pass at :53 already requires `app` to be a non-empty array of tables, so the path can't be reached today, which fits the finding's own low-severity, latent-only framing.

claim: `discover` filters on `Path::is_file()`, which turns any stat error (ELOOP on a self-referencing `Flockfile.toml` symlink, EACCES on the directory) into `false`, so that name is skipped silently. A lower-priority file such as `flockfile.json` can then win, or the caller sees "no Flockfile" instead of the real I/O error.
reason: `discover` returns `Option` and calls `p.is_file()` for each name. `is_file()` turns any metadata error (ELOOP, EACCES) into `false`, so a broken or unreadable higher-priority name is skipped silently: a lower-priority file can win, or the caller gets `None` instead of the I/O error.

claim: `name.parse::<Tz>().ok()` drops the chrono-tz error. The caller substitutes a typed `Timezone` error, so the failure still surfaces but the cause is lost. Low severity.
