reason: chrono-tz's parse error says only that the name is not a known zone, so `CronParseError::Timezone { name }` (cron.rs:68, message at :157) already keeps everything useful: the rejected name and why it was rejected.

claim: `render` uses `walk(..)?` and drops the returned `Completion::Unclosed`, so a value with an unclosed `{{` is silently truncated at that point. It is documented as "call `validate` first", but nothing enforces it for a caller that skips validation.
reason: `render` (template.rs:428) throws away the `Completion` that `walk` returns, and nothing in the code makes callers run `validate` first, so an unclosed `{{` is silently truncated; the doc comment admits this happens instead of preventing it.

claim: `TimeSearchLimitExceeded` is mapped to `Ok(None)`, "can never match again". That conflates "no match inside croner's search window" with "never matches". It is documented and probably intended. Low severity.
reason: At `cron.rs:115`, `next_after` maps croner's `TimeSearchLimitExceeded` to `Ok(None)`, and its doc says that means "can never match again"; but that error only means croner's bounded search window ran out, so a rare pattern that does match later would be reported as never matching, which is a real but low-severity conflation.

claim: `drifted_fields` returns `Vec::new()` when either `serde_json::to_value` call fails or yields a non-object, even though `self != other` was already established. A serialization failure therefore reads as "no drift". Practically unreachable for today's `AppConfig` shape.
reason: The empty-on-failure fallback is deliberate and documented in the code ("An empty result means no drift, or none could be computed"), and the finding itself says `AppConfig` can't reach it today, so it isn't a defect.

claim: `std::env::var(key).ok()` turns `VarError::NotUnicode` into "unset", so a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` silently falls back to `<home>/.shep` and `{{SHEP_HOME}}` expands to the wrong directory. `shep-cli/src/adopted.rs:73` reads the same variable with `var_os`, so the two disagree.
reason: `normalize` hands `paths::shep_home` the lookup `std::env::var(key).ok()`, so a non-UTF-8 `SHEP_HOME` comes back as `None`; `home_under` then falls back to `<home>/.shep` and `{{SHEP_HOME}}` expands there, while `adopted.rs:73` reads the same variable with `var_os` and gets the operator's real directory.

claim: `.map_err(|_| BadEnvValue(..))` drops the `UpDuration` parse error, so the operator sees the rejected `SHEP_MAX_CRON_SLEEP` value but not why it failed. The value is still reported, so this is minor.
reason: At config.rs:143, `.map_err(|_| ...)` throws away the `UpDuration` parse error, so `BadEnvValue` shows the rejected `SHEP_MAX_CRON_SLEEP` value but never says why it failed; the impact is minor, as the finding says.

claim: `literal` falls back to an empty string when a field has no `init.example`, so `shep init` writes a blank placeholder (`name = ""`). The sibling `blurb` panics on a missing blurb, so a missing example goes unnoticed while a missing blurb does not.
reason: `literal` (scaffold.rs:422-431) quietly falls back to `String::new()` when a field has no real default and no `init.example`, and nothing in scaffold.rs checks that examples are present, so a missing example ships a blank placeholder while a missing blurb panics.

claim: `parse_declared` uses `.unwrap_or_default()` on the `app` array and again at lines 73 and 78. If the value pass ever disagrees with the `RawFlockfile` pass, the declared-key sets come back empty, which reads as "this app declared nothing" rather than as an error. The comment at lines 55-58 argues it cannot happen, and nothing checks that.
reason: The two passes can disagree: `AppConfig` is a derived serde struct under `#[serde(rename = "app")]`, and derived structs also accept sequence form, so a document like `"app": [["web", ...]]` passes `RawFlockfile`, then `as_object` returns `None` and the app silently reports no declared keys; the comment's assumption is untested and not fully true.

claim: `render_positional` binds `let _: Result<Completion, Infallible>`, discarding `Completion::Unclosed` the same way as `render`. The output is truncated at an unclosed `{{`. `normalize` compares two such truncated strings at `resolved_app.rs:205`, so it could judge them "different" or "same" from partial text. That is only reachable if validation is skipped.
reason: `normalize` runs `validate_template` on `out_file`/`err_file` at resolved_app.rs:177 and returns early on error, before the comparison at :205, so an unclosed `{{` can never reach `render_positional` there; the truncation is also a documented precondition.

claim: `.as_str().unwrap_or_default()` treats a field with a missing `init.group` as group `""`, which sorts it last with no signal. The doc calls this deliberate for a future field, and `every_field_carries_a_group_and_a_blurb` is the only guard.
reason: The fallback is documented as intentional (GROUP_ORDER doc, line 84). The test `every_field_carries_a_group_and_a_blurb` fails when a field has a missing or unknown group, so no field can sort last without a signal in any build that passes tests.

claim: `.map_err(|_| BadPort{..})` discards the `ParseIntError`, so "empty", "non-numeric" and "out of u16 range" all read as "not a valid u16". The whole target is still named, so this is minor.
reason: `parse_port` throws away the `ParseIntError`, so a non-numeric port and an out-of-range port produce the same `BadPort` error; the finding is wrong about the empty case, though, because an empty port is caught earlier at line 324 and reported as `MissingPort`, and since the full target is still named the impact is minor.

claim: `kahn` does `break` when no node is ready, which drops every remaining node from `stages`, so those sheep are never started. The comment says a stall is impossible because cycles are lifted out first. A `debug_assert!` would state that invariant instead of assuming it.
reason: The `break` in `kahn` can't be reached: before `kahn` runs (lines 168 and 177), Tarjan's `knots` pulls out every strongly connected component, including self-loops, and `depends_on_a_cycle` pulls out every node that depends on one, so each remaining set is acyclic and no sheep is dropped. Adding a `debug_assert!` would only harden the code; there is no bug to fix.

claim: `parse_timezone_name` does `.parse::<Tz>().ok()` and discards the parser error. `CronSchedule::parse` rebuilds a typed error from the name alone, so nothing is lost there. A caller that gets `None` can only re-derive a reason from the name.
reason: chrono-tz's `Tz::from_str` error only says the name isn't a known IANA zone, so the name alone carries everything it would have said, and both `pub(super)` callers (cron.rs:68 and resolved_app.rs:225) build a typed error from the name, so discarding the error loses nothing.

claim: `report_fds` maps a timeout to `PumpReport::Unresponsive`, which is left out of `ParkedPumps`, but a late `ReportFds` still parks the pump (`log_file.rs:487-491`), so `resume()` is never sent and that sheep's log pump stops reading its child's output after the handover is refused.
reason: At log_file.rs:491 the pump sets `self.parked = true` before it answers, and it ignores a failed `done.send`, so a pump that answers after the 2s deadline (a slow flush, or a queued `ReportFds` read late) stays parked while `report_fds` has already returned `Unresponsive`, which is never added to `ParkedPumps`, so no `Resume` is ever sent.

claim: `spawn_adopted` aborts on the first `install_adopted` error, so sheep already installed keep tasks while the actor never runs, and sheep still in `flock` are dropped without a reaper wait, leaving their adopted children unsupervised and unreaped.
reason: The only production caller (`boot/mod.rs:275`) turns the error into a fatal `BootError::Adopt`, so the daemon exits. When it exits, the tasks it spawned die with it and init adopts and reaps the orphaned children, so the partial state never outlives the process.

claim: `install_adopted` returns `AdoptError::Spec` via `?` when a carried sheep's config fails `normalize`, before `runner.adopt` and before the reaper has its pid, so the live inherited child is never waited on.
reason: The `?` does return before `runner.adopt`, but the error then goes up through `spawn_adopted` (builder.rs:108) into `boot/mod.rs:275` as `BootError::Adopt`, which stops the boot, so no running daemon ever holds an unwaited child; once the process exits, init adopts and reaps the orphan.

claim: `reopen_logs` turns a dropped ack (`ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))`) into success, so a pump that dies after taking `LogCtl::Reopen` leaves a sheep writing nowhere while `spawn_reopen_task` reports Ok; `flush_logs` at line 119 has the same pattern.
reason: The docs at logs.rs:46-47 and :105-107 say this is deliberate: a dropped ack means the pump is gone, so nothing is left writing through it for reopen or flush to fix, and a pump dying is a separate failure that returning Err here would not surface or cure.

claim: `overridden_for` uses `overrides::get(..).ok().flatten()...unwrap_or_default()`, so an override-store read or parse error is dropped with no log and every sibling instance inherits a blank `overridden` cache, unlike `secret_view` just above, which logs.
reason: The doc comment deliberately chooses an empty answer on a store failure (worst case is a blank CFG cell), but `.ok()` also throws the error away without the `tracing::warn!` that `secret_view` emits, and later siblings copy that blank `overridden` from the first live slot, so the finding is accurate though low severity.

claim: `install_adopted` returns `AdoptError::Runner` when `runner.adopt(...)` fails, after the carried pipes and log fds are dropped and with no sheep task or slot, leaving a live child nothing waits on.
reason: The `AdoptError::Runner` is not handled per sheep: `spawn_adopted` passes it up with `?` (builder.rs:108), and boot/mod.rs:276 turns it into a fatal `BootError::Adopt`, so the whole daemon quits. No running shepherd is left with a child it ignores; the inherited children are re-parented to init, which reaps them.

claim: `handle_set_sheep_field` discards the `reached_spec` error with `.ok()` after the override store is written, so a field that cannot reach the running spec is reported only as pending, with no reason.
reason: The `.ok()` at line 532 comes before the override store is written, not after, and it is a deliberate, commented choice that mirrors `apply_one`: a normalize failure there means the app needs a restart, not that the request is invalid, so the field is parked as pending by design.

claim: `spawn_handover_task` does `let _ = reply.send(Ok((candidates, blob, parked)))`, so if the requester dropped its receiver, the unsent `ParkedPumps` is dropped and every pump that answered `ReportFds` stays parked with nobody to resume it.
reason: The only production caller, `hand_over_now` in `boot/handover.rs:158` (run from the SIGHUP task), awaits the reply with no timeout or select, so the receiver is dropped only if that task itself is aborted during shutdown, and then nothing is left to resume anyway.

claim: `apply_one` turns the `reached_spec` error into `.ok()`, so the reason a Live/NextSpawn change could not be applied is dropped with no log or refusal text, and `park_all` silently changes what is reported as applied versus pending.
reason: The `.ok()` is deliberate and documented at lines 236-239: when normalize rejects the reaching subset (for example, `watch` without `cwd`), the load parks instead of refusing. `park_all` then puts every field in pending, and if even the parked config can't be built, `parked_failed` pushes an explicit refusal, so no change is misreported as applied; only the normalize error text itself goes unused.

claim: `extra_restart` discards the `mpsc::Sender::send` result with `let _ =`, so a memory-breach or liveness-failure restart that fails to reach the mailbox is lost with no log; this is reachable only when the actor is already gone.
reason: The send fails only once the supervisor actor has dropped its receiver, which means the engine is shutting down and there is nothing left to restart; dropping the request there matches the documented behavior ('Silently does nothing… there is no reply'), so nothing is actually lost.

claim: `adoptable_child` drops the `std::process::Child` from `.spawn()` without a wait, relying on the adopted flock's reaper, so any adopt test that panics before adoption or `sup.shutdown()` leaves an unreaped shell child (test only; this also covers `tests/adopt_restart.rs:37`).
reason: The claim is accurate: `adoptable_child` drops the `Child` from `.spawn()` without waiting, and its doc comment says the adopted flock's reaper is meant to collect the status, so a test that panics before adoption or shutdown leaves the child unreaped until the test binary exits. The child is still a live process group running the script (e.g. `sleep 30`), but it is test-only and its stdio is null, so the harness cannot hang on it and the impact is minor. I did not check `tests/adopt_restart.rs:37`: that path does not exist under `crates/shep-daemon`.

claim: in `handle_scale`, `if let Some(recounted) = with_count(parked, achieved)` has no else and `with_count` is `normalize(..).ok()`, so a normalize failure silently leaves a parked config with a stale instance count (the same fallback is at line 178 via `.unwrap_or(parked)`).
reason: `normalize` can reject a count change on its own: a parked config written for 1 instance, with a fixed `out_file` and no `merge_logs`, fails `SharedLogPath` once `achieved` is above 1. Neither line 178 nor line 197 reports that failure, so the parked config keeps its stale `instances` with no signal.

claim: the `sleep 30` shell from `std::process::Command` has its `Child` handle dropped, so if `.expect("a carried flock installs")` panics before the SIGKILL, the child is never killed or waited on (test only).
reason: At adopt.rs:191 the `Child` is dropped without being killed, so if `spawn_adopted(...).expect(...)` panics, nothing sends SIGKILL and the `sleep 30` shell is left running for up to 30s as an unreaped orphan; the effect is small and limited to a test that is already failing.

claim: `shutdown` discards `rx.await` with `let _ =`, so if the actor drops the `Shutdown` reply before the kill-ladder aggregation completes, the caller cannot tell that live children may remain.
reason: The actor drops the `Shutdown` reply only if the actor task itself ends. `shutdown` is documented as a no-op when the actor is gone (handle.rs:730). `begin_shutdown` (actor_exit.rs:220) always sends the reply directly or hands it to a `PendingReply` for the kill-ladder aggregation, so no ordinary path drops it early. That leaves only a hypothetical actor panic, which the unit-returning API was deliberately not built to report.

claim: `a_carried_pending_delete_deregisters_on_the_next_exit` has the same dropped-`Child` pattern, so a panic before the SIGKILL leaves the process running and unreaped (test only).
reason: At adopt.rs:247 the `Child` is dropped without killing it, and dropping a std `Child` never kills the process, so if `spawn_adopted(...).expect` panics before the SIGKILL, the `sleep 30` shell keeps running and is never reaped.

claim: `a_carried_drainee_is_capped_by_graceful_timeout_not_kill_timeout` spawns a `trap '' TERM; sleep 300` child and reaps it only via `sup.shutdown()` at the end, so a failing assertion or `flock_until` panic earlier leaves a 300-second TERM-ignoring process behind (test only).
reason: The only way the drainee dies is the supervisor's escalation or `sup.shutdown()`, and the child ignores TERM. If `flock_until` panics, which is exactly what happens when the escalation regresses, the test unwinds before shutdown and leaves the adopted `sleep 300` process (it runs in its own process group and has no kill-on-drop guard) orphaned for up to five minutes.

claim: `apply_one` calls `with_count(..)`, which is `normalize(..).ok()`, so when the achieved count does not normalize, the recorded `app` becomes None with the error dropped and the muster roll stays on the old count.
reason: The only count-dependent checks in `normalize` are ZeroInstances and SharedLogPath (which only applies above 1 instance). `merged` already normalized at its own count, and the achieved count is at least min(running, target) ≥ 1 because a scale-down never falls short. So `with_count` cannot fail here, and the `None` path cannot be reached in practice.

claim: in `a_carried_manual_restart_respawns_and_keeps_its_origin`, `sup.shutdown()` runs only on the success path, so a failed assertion or timeout at lines 110-138 leaves the real `sleep 30` respawn running and unreaped (test only).
reason: `sup.shutdown().await` at line 141 is the only cleanup, and there is no Drop guard or scope guard, so a panic in any earlier `expect` or `assert` skips it and the respawned `sleep 30` is left running for up to 30 seconds; the effect is minor and limited to the test.

claim: discarded-error: `if let Some(recounted) = with_count(parked, achieved)` has no else or log. A parked config that fails to re-normalize keeps a stale `instances` while `spec` moves to `achieved`, and nothing is reported, unlike `apply_one`'s `parked_failed` refusal.
reason: `with_count` (config_merge.rs:299) turns the `normalize` error into `None` with `.ok()`, and line 197 has no else branch, so a parked config that fails validation at the new count (for example an instance-count-dependent check the parked config trips but `stored` passes) keeps its old `instances` while `spec` moves to `achieved`, with no reply error or log, unlike the refusal path used elsewhere.

claim: discarded-error: `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))` reports a reopen as successful when the pump drops its `done` sender without answering. A pump that died mid-reopen leaves the sheep writing to a stale or unlinked file while the operator sees Ok.
reason: The sheep writes into a pipe that the pump drains, not into the log file directly, so a dropped `done` means the pump task has ended and nothing is left writing to the old file; the doc comment on `reopen_logs` states this no-pump-means-success rule on purpose.

claim: unreaped-child: `install_adopted` returns early with `?` when `runner.adopt` refuses a sheep, and `builder.rs:108` (`spawn_adopted`) propagates it. Sheep already installed keep running with no supervisor, and those still queued in `flock` are dropped with their pids, so nothing waits on or kills those children. The `normalize` `?` at `actor_spawn.rs:418` leaks the same way.
reason: The unsupervised flock is deliberate and documented: an `AdoptError` from `spawn_adopted` becomes `BootError::Adopt` (boot/mod.rs:276), the successor exits without serving, and the flock keeps running with no shepherd. `boot/error.rs:89` spells this out to the operator ("The flock is still running and nothing is supervising it" … `shep muster`), and the test doc at `boot/handover.rs:289-293` says the same, so this is the designed failure mode rather than a leak.

claim: discarded-error: `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))` has the same problem on flush. A pump that dies after accepting `Flush` counts as flushed, then `truncate_log` runs and `Ok(matched)` is returned though the owed bytes may never have landed.
reason: The flush exists only so that no stale bytes land after the truncate. A pump that dies after accepting `Flush` can never write again, so treating the dropped ack as flushed still leaves the file correctly emptied, and returning `Ok(matched)` is the right result.

claim: discarded-error: `with_count(&parked, achieved).unwrap_or(parked)` swallows the `normalize` failure (`.ok()` at `config_merge.rs:302`). The stale parked config with the old instance count goes to every new slot with no log or refusal.
reason: `normalize` refuses a count above 1 when `merge_logs` is false and `out_file`/`err_file` lacks `{{instance}}` (SharedLogPath, `resolved_app.rs:198`); a parked config normalized at `instances = 1` can therefore fail `with_count` after a scale-up even though the live spec passed, and `unwrap_or(parked)` then puts the stale count on the new slots with no log or refusal.

claim: unreaped-child: the `JoinHandle` from `tokio::spawn(run_sheep(...))` is dropped. A panic in `run_sheep` or `kill_process`, or an abort at shutdown, drops `proc` mid-flight, so the child is neither killed nor waited on. No `Msg::Exited` reaches the actor, and no `kill_on_drop` or `Drop` impl covers it.
reason: `spawn_sheep_task` drops the `JoinHandle`, `TokioProc` has no `Drop` impl, and nothing sets `kill_on_drop`, so if `run_sheep` panics the child is never killed and `Msg::Exited` never reaches the actor, leaving its slot stuck. Children surviving a runtime abort at shutdown may be intentional, because handover adopts them, so the panic path is the real defect.

claim: unreaped-child: `adoptable_child` spawns a real `/bin/sh -c "sleep 30"` (or `sleep 300`) and drops the `std::process::Child` without `wait` or `kill`. A case that panics or times out before shutdown, or never adopts the pid, orphans it and leaves a zombie. The callers are `adopt_restart.rs:27` and `:88`, and `adopt_swap.rs:278`, `336`, `337`, `408`, `409`, `476` and `540`. `adopt_swap.rs:476` uses `trap '' TERM; sleep 300`, which survives SIGTERM for 5 minutes.
reason: `adoptable_child` (mod.rs:959) is meant to drop the `Child` so the adopted flock's reaper can collect it, but no guard kills the process group when a case panics, times out, or never adopts it. The detached group then outlives the case: up to 30s for `sleep 30`, 300s for the TERM-ignoring drainee at adopt_swap.rs:476. If it exits while the test binary is still running, it sits as a zombie until the binary exits.

claim: discarded-error: the same `reached_spec(...).ok()` pattern. `handle_set_sheep_field` answers `pending: true` for a Live field with no reason for the downgrade. Lower severity.
reason: At actor_pane.rs:532, `reached_spec(...).ok()` throws away the normalize error string, so a Live field that falls back to park_all comes back as `pending: true` with no reason given to the operator; the comment says this is intentional, so it is a real but low-severity diagnosability gap and not a correctness bug.

claim: discarded-error: `reached_spec(...).ok()` drops the `Err(String)` explaining why the subset would not normalize. `park_all` silently downgrades every field to pending with no log or refusal text. Lower severity, since the fields are still reported as pending.
reason: At line 240, `reached_spec(...).ok()` throws away the `Err` text, and the `park_all` path that follows never logs it or adds it to `refusals`, so the operator never learns why every field was parked; the comment says parking is deliberate, but losing the reason is a real, low-severity diagnostic gap.

claim: discarded-error: `overrides::get(..).ok().flatten()` drops an override-store read error with no log, so the sheep's overridden list silently shows empty. The sibling `secret_view` warns on the same failure. Cosmetic only.
reason: `overridden_for` (actor_spawn.rs:103-105) throws away the `overrides::get` error with `.ok().flatten()` and logs nothing, while the sibling `secret_view` logs a `tracing::warn!` on the same kind of read failure; the doc comment says an empty answer is intended, so the missing log is a real but cosmetic gap.

claim: `overrides::get(..).ok().flatten()` drops the read error with no log (unlike `secret_view`, which warns) and the result is cached in `ProcessEntry::overridden`, so a transient store failure blanks the CFG marker until the next load with no trace.
reason: At actor_spawn.rs:103, `overridden_for` throws away the `overrides::get` error without logging it, while `secret_view` at actor_spawn.rs:78 logs a warning. The empty result is stored in `entry.overridden`, and sibling entries reuse it, so a temporary read failure leaves the CFG cell blank with nothing in the logs.

claim: `signals.try_send(..).is_err()` collapses `Full` and `Closed` into `SignalOutcome::NotRunning`, so a live sheep with a full signal queue is reported not running and the operator's signal is not delivered (documented as intentional, weaker).
reason: At line 132, `try_send(..).is_err()` does treat `TrySendError::Full` the same as `Closed` and reports `SignalOutcome::NotRunning`, so the signal is dropped; the comment defends this by assuming a full queue means the sheep is dying, but the code never checks that, so a live but busy sheep gets the wrong outcome.

claim: `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))` (same at line 119 for flush) turns a pump that dropped its `done` sender without answering into success, so `reopen`/`flush` can report success to a logrotate `postrotate` while a pump still holds the renamed inode or unflushed bytes; it is unlogged.
reason: The pump always answers `done` once it handles a Reopen or Flush (`log_file.rs:442-480`), so the sender is only dropped unanswered when the pump task has ended or the message sat unread in its queue as it shut down; in both cases the pump's files are closed and it holds no renamed inode or unflushed bytes, which is the documented, deliberate success case.

claim: `adoptable_child` spawns a real `/bin/sh` (`sleep 30`, `trap '' TERM; sleep 300`) and drops the `Child` without wait/kill, so a case that panics before the adopted reaper takes the pid leaves the child running and later a zombie.
reason: `adoptable_child` drops the `Child` and keeps only its pid, with no kill guard, so any case that panics before adoption leaves `sleep 30` or the TERM-ignoring `sleep 300` running as an orphan; the comment's own mention of a child that outlives a failing case admits this.

claim: `with_count(&parked, achieved).unwrap_or(parked)` (and the `if let Some(recounted)` at line 197) silently swallows a `normalize` failure and keeps the parked config at a stale instance count, which the adjacent comment calls drift that never clears.
reason: A parked config can differ from the live spec: for example, it can have `instances = 1`, a fixed `out_file` with no `{{instance}}`, and `merge_logs = false`; scaling to 2 or more then fails `normalize` with `SharedLogPath`, `with_count` returns `None`, and the parked count stays stale with no error, which is the drift the comment says never clears.

claim: on `REPORT_DEADLINE` the timeout drops `ack` and returns `Unresponsive`, but a wedged pump that later serves the queued `ReportFds` parks itself while `parked_pump` is `None`, so it is never resumed despite the "never parked" doc.
reason: The pump sets `self.parked = true` unconditionally when it serves `ReportFds` (log_file.rs:491) and ignores a failed `done.send`, so a pump that was slow past `REPORT_DEADLINE` but got the queued message, or was already mid-drain, parks with nobody holding its `log_ctl` to send `Resume`, and stops reading its sheep's streams for good.

claim: `let _ = reply.send(Ok((candidates, blob, parked)))` drops the `ParkedPumps` if the caller stopped waiting, so pumps that already answered `ReportFds` stay parked with nothing to send `Resume`, and those sheep's stdout/stderr stop being read.
reason: The only caller, `hand_over_now` (boot/handover.rs:158), is awaited by the SIGHUP task (boot/signals.rs:179), which has no timeout, select or cancellation. The receiver is therefore dropped only when the runtime itself is shutting down, and the pumps die with it, so no live daemon is left holding parked pumps.

claim: a SIGTERM-immune `trap '' TERM; sleep 300` child is only killed by `sup.shutdown()` at line 527, so a panic in `flock_until` or a failed `spawn_adopted` leaves it running for 300s.
reason: `adoptable_child` returns a bare pid with no kill-on-drop guard, and `sup.shutdown()` is the only cleanup, so a panic in `flock_until` or in `spawn_adopted().expect` skips it and leaves the TERM-ignoring `sleep 300` orphaned in its own process group; stdio is nulled, so it wastes a process but does not hang the harness.

claim: the raw `std::process::Command::new("/bin/sh")` child keeps inherited stdio and has no `process_group(0)`, unlike `adoptable_child`, so if `spawn_adopted` or the SIGKILL `.expect` fails, `sleep 30` is left unreaped and can hold the harness pipe open and hang the run.
reason: The test at adopt.rs:191 builds its `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 30'` child by hand, leaving stdio inherited and skipping `process_group(0)`. The shared `adoptable_child` helper in tests/mod.rs:960 sets both specifically so that a child outliving a failed case can't keep the harness's stdout pipe open and hang the run. If `spawn_adopted` or the SIGKILL `.expect` panics, this child is left alive for up to 30s holding that pipe.

claim: same pattern as line 191 (inherited stdio, no process group, `child` never waited), so a failure before the kill at line 268 leaks `sleep 30`.
reason: If `spawn_adopted(...).expect` at line 250 panics, the test never reaches the SIGKILL at line 268; the `sleep 30` child then runs as an orphan for up to 30 s, still holding the inherited stdio, because nothing kills or waits on it (the same pattern as line 191).

claim: the `sleep 30` child and the replacement `TokioRunner` spawns are reaped only by `sup.shutdown()` at line 321, so a `flock_until` timeout or failed assert before it leaks both.
reason: `adoptable_child` detaches a `sleep 30` into its own process group without a kill guard, and `TokioRunner` spawns without `kill_on_drop`, so a panic from `flock_until` or the asserts skips `sup.shutdown()` and orphans both; the damage is bounded because the sleep exits on its own after 30s and has null stdio, so it cannot hang a piped harness.

claim: the two adopted children are cleaned up only by `sup.shutdown()` at line 462, so the timeout `expect` at line 451 or the asserts at lines 454-460 skip it.
reason: `adoptable_child` returns a bare pid with no drop guard, so if the timeout `expect` or an assert panics before `sup.shutdown()`, both `sleep 30` children are left running as orphans for up to 30 seconds; stdio is nulled, so nothing hangs, but the processes do leak.

claim: both adopted `sleep 30` children (drainee and replacement) are killed only if the test reaches `sup.shutdown()` at line 394, so the 20s `await_event` timeout, the `flock_until` panic or the asserts at lines 379-392 leak them.
reason: `adoptable_child` returns only a bare pid, with no kill-on-drop guard. The only thing that kills either `sleep 30` group is `sup.shutdown()` at the end, so a timeout, a panic or a failed assert leaves both children running for up to 30s. They do exit on their own after that, and their stdio is null, so the leak is bounded and can't hang the test harness.

claim: the adopted `sleep 30` child and the reload-spawned replacement are cleaned up only by `sup.shutdown()` at line 575, so a `reload` expect failure, a `flock_until` panic or an earlier assert leaks them.
reason: `adoptable_child` returns a bare pid and there is no Drop guard, so both processes are killed only by the `sup.shutdown()` call at the end. If the test panics before that line, the `sleep 30` child and its replacement are left running, though each one exits by itself within 30 seconds, and the null stdio means they don't hold the test harness open.

claim: `let _ = handle.start(...)` (and `let _ = handle.restart(...)` at line 153) drops the result with no comment, so an unexpected `SpawnFailed` from an exhausted script pool goes unnoticed and the invariants can pass for the wrong reason.
reason: `SCRIPT_POOL` is set to 512, and the comment above it (interleaving.rs:66-73) says a run can make fewer than 200 spawns and explains why running out would matter, so the pool cannot run dry within these steps; the `start`/`restart` calls also return errors in normal cases (such as restarting an empty flock) that this test does not check, so dropping the result is deliberate.

claim: `let _ = t.await;` discards each stop task's `JoinError`, so a panic inside one of the eight spawned `stop` calls is swallowed and the test only checks event timing.
reason: `let _ = t.await;` throws away both the `JoinError` and the `stop` result, so a panic or error in any of the eight stop tasks goes unnoticed and the test passes on event timing alone.

claim: `sup.shutdown()` is reached only if every assertion before it passes, so a failed timeout or assert at lines 110-138 leaves the respawned real `sleep 30` running with no kill or wait.
reason: The spawned sheep's only cleanup is the `sup.shutdown().await` at line 141, and nothing in the supervisor's spawn path kills children on drop, so a panic from any earlier timeout or assert leaves the respawned `sleep 30` orphaned for up to 30 seconds.

claim: `let _ = h.stop(...)` inside detached `tokio::spawn` tasks (also line 284 for `list_checked`) drops both the `Result` and the `JoinHandle`, so a panic or error from a flooded command is invisible.
reason: The spawned stop/list_checked calls exist only to flood the mailbox for a deadlock test whose single assertion is the Stop event, so their results are deliberately irrelevant (concurrent stops on an already-stopping sheep can legitimately error), and discarding them is intentional fire-and-forget load, not a hidden failure.

claim: `while let Ok(ev) = rx.try_recv()` also stops on `Lagged`/`Closed`, so the "no GHOST RESPAWN" and "no Online" absence assertions in `shutdown_ignores_a_pending_restart_timer` and `shutdown_ignores_a_pending_readiness_wait` pass vacuously if events were dropped.
reason: Both tests use a 1024-slot bus and emit only a handful of events, so `Lagged` can't happen here; tokio also delivers every buffered message before it returns `Closed`, so the drain still sees every event and the absence assertions aren't vacuous.

claim: The 2s timeout covers `send` plus `ack`, and treats a timeout as "never parked". If the `ReportFds` send succeeded but the pump was slow, it later sets `parked = true` (`tokio_runner/log_file.rs:491`) and its ack is discarded. Nobody sends `Resume`, so the pump stops reading that sheep's pipes for good on an abandoned handover.
reason: On timeout `report_fds` returns `Unresponsive` and leaves that pump out of `ParkedPumps`, but the `ReportFds` it already queued still runs later and sets `parked = true` (`log_file.rs:491`); the handover is then refused as `PumpUnresponsive`, so `ParkedPumps::resume` never sends that pump a `Resume` and it stops reading its sheep's pipes for good.

claim: `install_adopted(...)?` aborts the whole adoption on the first error, so every carried sheep not yet installed keeps a live pid that is never handed to the reaper or a sheep task. Those children run unsupervised and become zombies when they exit. `AdoptError`'s own doc admits "that is which process is now unsupervised".
reason: The `?` error goes up through `boot/mod.rs:275` as `BootError::Adopt` and the whole successor daemon exits, so the claimed failure doesn't happen: sheep not yet installed are not left beside a running supervisor, init reaps the orphaned children rather than leaving zombies, and the already-installed ones lose supervision too, which makes this a deliberate fail-closed boot that the `AdoptError` doc acknowledges.

claim: `let _ = ctl.try_send(SheepCtl::Kill{..})` ignores `Full` and `Closed` after `slot.manual` is already set at line 321. If the sheep task ended without sending `Msg::Exited` (for example it panicked), the marker and its pending reply never resolve, and a `shutdown` waiting on that sheep hangs.
reason: Ignoring `try_send` is not what causes the hang: `Full` means a `Kill` is already queued, and `Closed` means the sheep task ended after sending its single `Msg::Exited`, which will clear the marker. A panicked sheep task (`sheep.rs:97-110`) never sends `Msg::Exited` whatever `claim_manual` does, so that failure is a gap in the task's panic handling, not a bug at `actor_lifecycle.rs:328`.

claim: `kill_process` awaits `tx.send(Shutdown)` outside its grace timeout (`kill.rs:41`, capacity 32). If a wedged child has filled that channel, the ladder never reaches SIGKILL, so the child is never killed or reaped.
reason: At `kill.rs:41`, `tx.send(ShepherdMessage::Shutdown).await` runs before the grace timeout, with nothing bounding it. The only thing draining the channel is the writer task in `pump.rs:466`, which blocks on `write_all` once a child that isn't reading has filled the socket buffer. After that the 32-slot channel fills, `send` never returns, and `kill_tree()`/SIGKILL is never reached.

claim: A carried config that no longer normalizes returns `AdoptError::Spec` before `runner.adopt`, so that sheep's live process is never reaped. The pending-config path at line 450 deliberately avoids stranding a live flock, but this path does not.
reason: `install_adopted` returns `AdoptError::Spec` through `?` in `spawn_adopted` (builder.rs:108), and boot/mod.rs:275 turns that into a fatal `BootError::Adopt`. A successor whose tighter normalization rejects one carried config therefore fails to boot and strands the whole inherited flock unreaped, not just that one sheep. The pending-config path explicitly avoids this outcome.

claim: The same `unwrap_or(Ok(()))` on flush treats an unanswered flush as landed, and `spawn_flush_task` then truncates the file anyway.
reason: The behaviour is deliberate and documented: an unanswered ack means the pump has exited, and a pump that is gone owes no bytes. `spawn_flush_task` runs `truncate_log` whether or not the flush failed, so an `Ok` from `unwrap_or` cannot cause a truncate that would not otherwise have happened.

claim: `let _ = reply.send(Ok((candidates, blob, parked)))` discards the error. If the requester was dropped, `ParkedPumps` (no `Drop`, only an async `resume`) is lost with it, and every pump that parked stays parked.
reason: The only requester is `hand_over_now`, called from the SIGHUP task in boot/signals.rs:179. That task awaits the reply directly, with no timeout or `select!`, and resumes `parked` on every refusal path, so the receiver can only drop if the whole signal task is aborted while the daemon is tearing down, and at that point parked pumps no longer matter.

claim: `overrides::get(..).ok().flatten()` drops the store error with no log, unlike `secret_view` at line 78, so a corrupt or unreadable store silently blanks the CFG cell.
reason: At line 104, `overridden_for` turns any `overrides::get` error into an empty list with no `tracing::warn!`, while `secret_view` at line 78 logs its store error; the doc comment accepts the blank CFG cell as the worst case but gives no reason for dropping the log, so this is a low-severity gap in what operators can see rather than a correctness bug.

claim: `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))` reports a reopen as successful when the pump took the request and dropped its `done` sender without answering.
reason: This is intended and documented at logs.rs:47-48: a dropped acknowledgement means no pump is left to reopen anything. The real pump always calls `done.send(result)` once it takes a `Reopen` (tokio_runner/log_file.rs:442-459), so the sender is dropped unanswered only when the pump has exited or its task was aborted, not because a reopen failed.

claim: `let _ = actor_tx.send(Msg::Exited{..})` drops the exit outcome silently when the mailbox is closed (also lines 108, 154, 172). This is benign at shutdown but leaves no trace after the early return at `builder.rs:108`.
reason: The early return at `builder.rs:108` (`install_adopted(...)?`) drops the actor and its receiver while the sheep already installed keep running, so their `Msg::Exited` sends at `sheep.rs:100`/`108` do go nowhere. But that path returns an `AdoptError` to the caller, so the failure itself is recorded; only the individual exit outcomes are lost, and whether that matters depends on how the caller handles the orphaned flock, which I did not trace.

claim: `reached_spec(..).ok()` drops the same error, so an operator's field edit falls back to parking with no reason logged.
reason: At actor_pane.rs:532, `reached_spec(..).ok()` throws away the `Err(String)` that describes the failure. The code parks the edit because `next_spec.is_none()`, but it never logs the reason. actor_config.rs:240 drops the same error in the same way.

claim: `adoptable_child` drops the `std::process::Child`. If a test fails before the adopted flock's reaper takes over, that `sleep` is left unreaped, and `adopt_swap.rs:476` uses a `sleep 300`.
reason: The helper drops the `Child` and returns only the pid, with no kill guard. If a case panics before the adopted flock's ladder kills it (for example, at `.spawn_adopted(...).unwrap()` or at an assertion), the `trap '' TERM; sleep 300` in its own process group keeps running for up to 5 minutes. Output is nulled, so it does not hang the harness. Keeping the `Child` would not fix it either, because dropping a std `Child` does not kill the process; the fix needs a kill-on-drop guard.

claim: `reached_spec(..).ok()` discards why the subset spec failed, and the "could not be parked" refusal at line 333 never names the cause.
reason: When the subset spec fails at line 240, the code parks the config by design and does not refuse (see the comment at lines 236-239); the refusal at line 333 comes from `parked_failed`, which is set when `with_count(&merged, count)` fails, not from the discarded `reached_spec` error, and that refusal does name its cause: the merged config does not hold at N instances.

claim: `let _ = t.await` discards the `JoinError` and the `stop` result, so a panicking stop task passes silently.
reason: At shutdown.rs:251, `let _ = t.await` discards both the JoinError and the stop result, so a panic inside `handle.stop` would not fail the test; ignoring the stop result may be deliberate since concurrent stops can race, but the JoinError should at least be unwrapped (e.g. `t.await.unwrap();`).

claim: The `/bin/sh` child is spawned with inherited stdio, and `mod.rs:966` warns that this hangs under a pipe. It is never waited on, so if `spawn_adopted(..).expect(..)` panics the child is left behind.
reason: At adopt.rs:191 the test spawns `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 30'` with inherited stdio and never waits on it. So if `spawn_adopted(..).expect(..)` panics before the SIGKILL, the orphaned shell keeps the harness's stdout pipe open for up to 30s, which is exactly the hang `tests/mod.rs:966` warns about. The `adoptable_child` helper there avoids it by nulling stdio.

claim: `let _ = handle.start(..)` discards the result (line 153 does the same for `restart`), so a failed start or restart in the property test is ignored.
reason: This is a property test over arbitrary interleavings. The ScriptedRunner scripts and readiness gates are drawn at random, so a start or restart that errors is an expected outcome. The test asserts invariants on the listing after every step, not whether each command succeeds, so discarding the result is deliberate.

claim: the Kill branch awaits `kill_process`, whose wait after SIGKILL (`kill.rs:47`) has no timeout, so a child that survives SIGKILL is never reaped, `Msg::Exited` never fires, and a pending stop, delete or shutdown reply hangs; `actor_reload_done.rs:139` admits the gap.
reason: `kill_process` (`kill.rs:54`) calls `proc.wait().await` after `kill_tree` with no timeout, so a child that SIGKILL cannot reap yet (for example one stuck in uninterruptible D-state I/O) keeps the sheep task at `sheep.rs:107` from sending `Msg::Exited`, and the comment at `actor_reload_done.rs:136-139` confirms that only reloads have a deadline for this gap, not stop, delete or shutdown.

claim: `overridden_for` turns an unreadable override store into an empty list with `.ok()` and no log, unlike `secret_view` at `:78`; the CFG column silently loses its `*` marks.
reason: `overridden_for` uses `.ok().flatten()` with no `tracing::warn!`, while `secret_view` directly above logs the path and error for the same kind of failure. The doc comment accepts the empty result on purpose but never explains why nothing is logged, so an unreadable overrides.json quietly blanks the CFG `*` marks and leaves no trace for the operator.

claim: `Command::Scale` has no `shutting_down` guard, unlike `Start`, `Restart` and `Reload`, so a scale-up during shutdown calls `spawn_fresh` and starts a child that `begin_shutdown`'s already-fixed `online` snapshot never kills or waits on (no test covers it).
reason: `handle_command` sends `Command::Scale` directly to `handle_scale`. Neither that function nor `spawn_fresh` checks `shutting_down`, but `Start`, `Restart`, `Reload` and `do_start_dog` all check it and give the same reason: a child spawned after shutdown begins is one the fixed shutdown aggregation cannot kill.

claim: `flush_logs` reads a dropped acknowledgement as success (`unwrap_or(Ok(()))`), so a pump that dies mid-flush is reported flushed and `truncate_log` then runs; `reopen_logs` at `:59` does the same for reopen.
reason: The documented, intentional contract is that a dropped acknowledgement means no pump is left, so a gone pump owes no bytes and truncation always runs anyway, even on a real flush error; reading the drop as success is by design, not a bug.

claim: `install_adopted` returns early on `AdoptError::Spec` (and at `:557` on `Runner`) before the sheep's live pid reaches the `AdoptedReaper`, and `builder.rs:108`'s `?` also drops every later sheep in `flock` unadopted, so those children are never waited on and earlier sheep's tasks are left detached. `boot/mod.rs:275` turns this into a `BootError`, so the impact depends on boot exiting.
reason: The early returns and the `?` at builder.rs:108 do skip the reaper, but `spawn_adopted`'s error turns into `BootError::Adopt`, which ends the successor shepherd during boot, so the orphaned children are reparented to init and reaped there, and the detached tasks die with the process.

claim: when `with_count` (`config_merge.rs:302`, `normalize(config).ok()`) fails, the parked config keeps its stale instance count with no log or refusal, which is the "drift that never clears" the comment above it warns about; `:178` falls back to the stale `parked` the same way.
reason: `normalize` has count-dependent refusals: `SharedLogPath` at `resolved_app.rs:198` fires only when `instances > 1` without `merge_logs`, so a parked config that normalized at 1 instance with a fixed `out_file` fails `with_count` when scaled up; both `:178` (`unwrap_or(parked)`) and `:197` then silently keep the stale count, with no log and no refusal.

claim: `handle_scale` (via `Command::Scale`, `actor_core.rs:104`) has no `shutting_down` guard, so a scale-up during shutdown calls `spawn_fresh` and starts a child that the shutdown's fixed `online` snapshot never kills; its sheep task is then orphaned when the actor loop breaks.
reason: `handle_scale` never checks `shutting_down`, and neither does `spawn_fresh`, so a scale-up arriving after `begin_shutdown` still spawns new instances; `Start`, `Reload`, `Restart` and `StartDog` are all guarded against exactly this case, with a comment in `actor_core.rs` saying the fixed shutdown snapshot cannot know to kill such a child.

claim: `reached_spec(...).ok()` drops the reason a partial config failed to normalize, so a load that parks everything reports its fields as `pending` with no explanation.
reason: When `reached_spec` fails, `park_all` succeeds and `parked_failed` stays false, so no refusal is pushed. Every field, Live ones included, then lands in `pending` and the normalize error is never surfaced (actor_config.rs:240, 380-395); the same `.ok()` pattern appears again at actor_pane.rs:532.

claim: `install_adopted(...)?` aborts the whole handover on the first error, dropping the actor and mailbox. The failing sheep and every sheep after it never reach `runner.adopt`, so no reaper waits on their live pids. The earlier sheep keep running unsupervised with no actor listening.
reason: `spawn_adopted` returns early on the first `install_adopted` error, and its only caller (`boot/mod.rs:275`) turns that into a fatal `BootError::Adopt`, so the successor daemon exits with no rollback while every inherited sheep's pid keeps running with no supervisor or reaper.

claim: `overrides::get(...).ok()` throws away the store error with no log, unlike `secret_view` a few lines above. The blank `overridden` is cached on the entry until the next load.
reason: At actor_spawn.rs:103, `.ok()` turns an override-store read error into an empty list with no log, while `secret_view` just above logs its store failure with `tracing::warn!`. Scale-up copies the value from a live sibling, so the blank `overridden` list persists until the next load. The doc comment says returning empty is deliberate, so the defect is the missing log line, not the fallback.

claim: `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))` turns a dropped reopen ack into success, so `shep reopen` can report a rotation done while a pump died before reopening its files.
reason: The code does this on purpose, and the doc comment on `reopen_logs` says so: a dropped ack means the pump has already exited, so no process is still writing to a rotated-away file and nothing needs reopening; the only real failure, a pump that answered but could not open a path again, still comes back as `Err`.

claim: `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))` reports a pump that dropped its ack mid-flush as success. `spawn_flush_task` then truncates the files anyway, so bytes the pump still owed are lost without an error.
reason: The pump at tokio_runner/log_file.rs:461-480 always sends on `done` once it handles a Flush, so the ack is only dropped when the pump task itself ends; that is the 'a pump that is gone owes no bytes' case the doc comment at logs.rs:106-108 accepts on purpose, and the truncate afterwards does not lose any byte that the flush would have saved.

claim: `normalize(carried.app())` failing returns `AdoptError::Spec` before `carried.pid()` is handed to the reaper, so an inherited live child is dropped with its pipes closed and nothing waits on it.
reason: The `?` at actor_spawn.rs:415 propagates through `spawn_adopted` (builder.rs:108) into `BootError::Adopt` (boot/mod.rs:276), so the whole successor boot fails and the daemon exits rather than carrying on with one sheep dropped, and the orphaned child is then reparented to init, which reaps it; so no child is left unwaited in a running shepherd.

claim: `reached_spec(...).ok()` drops the reason a config could not be applied and falls back to `park_all` without logging it; `actor_pane.rs:532` does the same.
reason: The `.ok()` is deliberate and commented at both sites: a reaching-field subset that fails `normalize` (for example `watch` without its `cwd`) is designed to park the config for the next respawn rather than refuse it, so the parked outcome is the reported result and the dropped error string is not a correctness defect.

claim: `let _ = ctl.try_send(SheepCtl::Kill{..})` ignores `Full` and `Closed` after `slot.manual` is already set. It is safe only because a `Closed` sheep task always has a `Msg::Exited` in flight, and nothing here checks that.
reason: Ignoring the `try_send` result is a documented design choice, not a bug: `Full` can only mean a `Kill` is already queued, because `slot.rs` keeps signals and `to_child` in separate mailboxes so `Kill` is the ctl mailbox's only occupant, and `Closed` means the sheep task has ended and its `Msg::Exited` is on the way to settle the `manual` marker, so no stop is lost.

claim: `let _ = t.await;` discards the `JoinError` from eight spawned `stop` tasks, so a panic in one passes the test silently.
reason: `let _ = t.await;` at shutdown.rs:251 throws away both the `JoinError` and the inner stop `Result`, so a panic in any of the eight spawned `stop` tasks goes unnoticed and the test still passes on the timing assertion alone.

claim: `overrides::get(...).ok().flatten()` discards the store's read error with no log, unlike `secret_view` beside it, so the CFG column silently goes blank.
reason: At actor_spawn.rs:103-105, `.ok()` throws away the override store's read error without logging it, while `secret_view` right above logs a `warn!` for the same kind of failure; the doc comment accepts a blank CFG cell as the fallback, but nothing explains why the error goes unlogged, so an operator has no signal that the store is unreadable.

claim: same `reached_spec(...).ok()` discard in `handle_set_sheep_field`; the operator gets `pending: true` and no reason.
reason: The `.ok()` discard is deliberate and commented at actor_pane.rs:527-531: a normalize failure on the partial spec means the app needs a restart, not that the request is invalid, which matches `apply_one`, and the parked config's differing fields still appear through the shared `pending` definition.

claim: `with_count` returns `normalize(config).ok()`, so the callers at actor_config.rs:254 and actor_scale.rs:178,197 all lose the reason, and the refusal text is a generic "does not hold at N instance(s)".
reason: `with_count` throws away the `normalize` error with `.ok()`, so actor_config.rs:334 can only report the generic "the merged config does not hold at {count} instance(s)" (the actor_scale.rs callers produce no refusal text; they just fall back quietly and also lose the reason).

claim: `let _ = ctl.try_send(SheepCtl::Kill { grace })` discards both `Full` and `Closed` after `slot.manual` is already set. It is safe only while `Kill` is the sole `ctl` message and `Msg::Exited` is guaranteed to follow, which is documented but not enforced.
reason: `SheepCtl` has exactly one variant (`Kill`, `types.rs:123`) and this arm runs only when `slot.manual` is `None`, so a `Full` error means a `Kill` is already queued and a `Closed` error means the sheep has exited; either way a `Msg::Exited` still follows, so nothing breaks today and the finding describes a possible future hazard rather than a current defect.

claim: `reached_spec(...).ok()` throws away the normalize error, so the `park_all` outcome reports fields as pending without saying why they could not reach the running process.
reason: At crates/shep-daemon/src/supervisor/actor_config.rs:240, `.ok()` throws away the `normalize` error string. When `park_all` is set, every field is reported only as `pending`, and no refusal or log records why the subset config failed (for example, `watch` without `cwd`), so the operator gets no cause.

claim: the `/bin/sh -c "sleep 30"` child (also at line 247) is spawned with inherited stdio and no process group, then dropped without a wait. If the test fails before the SIGKILL it leaves an unreaped `sleep 30` and can hang a piped `cargo test`. `adoptable_child` in tests/mod.rs:960 already avoids the stdio half.
reason: Both tests spawn `/bin/sh -c "sleep 30"` with inherited stdio and no `process_group(0)`, then drop the `Child` without waiting on it, so a panic before the SIGKILL (for example in `spawn_adopted(...).expect`) leaves the child holding the harness's stdout pipe. That stalls a piped `cargo test` for up to 30s, the case `adoptable_child` was written to avoid, and swapping in `adoptable_child("sleep 30")` fixes it.

claim: `adoptable_child` drops the `Child` unwaited and relies on the adopted flock's reaper, so a case that fails before adoption or before the kill leaves a zombie and a live child, up to 300s for the `trap '' TERM; sleep 300` case at adopt_swap.rs:476.
reason: `adoptable_child` returns only the pid and drops the `Child` with no kill guard, so a case that panics before the flock adopts or kills it (for example a failed `flock_until` in the drainee case) leaves the `trap '' TERM; sleep 300` shell running and unreaped for up to 300s; the child's null stdio stops it from hanging the harness, but nothing cleans it up.

claim: `let _ = t.await` discards the `JoinError` and the `stop` result from each of the eight spawned stop tasks, so a panic in one is invisible to the case.
reason: At shutdown.rs:251, `let _ = t.await` throws away both the JoinError and the inner `stop` Result, so a panic or error in any of the eight stop tasks never fails the test; the test only asserts on sheep b's timing.

claim: `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))` turns a dropped flush acknowledgement into success, so `truncate_log` runs anyway and unflushed bytes are lost silently.
reason: A dropped ack means the pump task is gone. The doc comment deliberately treats that as success (a gone pump owes no bytes), and `truncate_log` runs regardless of the flush result even on a real `FlushError`, so mapping the drop to `Ok` changes neither whether the truncate runs nor how many bytes are lost.

claim: `let _ = handle.start(..).await` (and `restart` at line 153) discards the `Result`, so the proptest model cannot tell a refused step from a broken one.
reason: The proptest checks state invariants rather than modelling each step's outcome. Scripted runners and empty selectors make errors legitimate results, and the listing checks after every step catch a broken supervisor whatever start or restart returned, the same Ok-only pattern `stop` and `delete` use.

claim: `let _ = reply.send(Ok((candidates, blob, parked)))` drops `ParkedPumps` if the caller is gone, so no `Resume` is sent and the parked log pumps stay stopped (only `boot/handover.rs:169` resumes them, and only after receiving the reply).
reason: The only caller, the SIGHUP task via `hand_over_now`, awaits the reply with no timeout or select, so the receiver disappears only when that task is aborted during daemon teardown, and at that point parked pumps no longer matter.

claim: `with_count(&parked, achieved).unwrap_or(parked)` swallows a normalize failure, so the parked config keeps the old instance count and `apply_one`'s `parked_failed` warning never fires here.
reason: The `parked_failed` warning belongs to `apply_one` in actor_config.rs, a separate path that `handle_scale` never runs through. A parked config was already normalized, so only its `instances` changes here, and a normalize failure is not a realistic outcome. Keeping the old parked config on failure also matches the `with_count` fallback a few lines below (line 196).

claim: `if let Some(recounted) = with_count(parked, achieved)` drops the `None` failure the same way, leaving the count drift uncorrected and unreported.
reason: `with_count` failing does silently leave the parked count stale, but `stored` was just normalized with the same `achieved` count (or the handler already returned), so `normalize` would fail on the parked config only if some instance-dependent validation treats it differently from `stored`, which is not shown to be reachable.

claim: the same `unwrap_or(Ok(()))` reports a pump that died mid-reopen as reopened.
reason: The doc comment on `reopen_logs` makes this deliberate: a dropped acknowledgement means no pump is left to write anywhere, so there is no stream going to a stale or missing file and nothing for the reopen to report; a pump dying is a separate failure that the reopen reply is not meant to cover.

claim: `signals.try_send(...).is_err()` treats a full 16-slot queue as `NotRunning` and drops the error, so a live but busy sheep is reported as not running.
reason: This is deliberate and documented: the comment at actor_actions.rs:133-135 says a full queue on a syscall-fast signal handler means the sheep task is dying, so `NotRunning` is the intended outcome, not a dropped error.

claim: `overrides::get(...).ok().flatten()` drops an override-store read error with no log, unlike `secret_view` at :78, so the CFG column comes out blank with no trace.
reason: `overridden_for` turns an `overrides::get` error into an empty list with `.ok().flatten()` and never logs it, while `secret_view` directly above logs with `tracing::warn!` when its store read fails; the doc comment says a blank CFG cell is acceptable but says nothing to justify dropping the error without a trace.

claim: `reached_spec(...).ok()` in `handle_set_sheep_field` drops the same error and surfaces only as `pending: true`, with no warning.
reason: At actor_pane.rs:532, `.ok()` throws away the `reached_spec` error string (for example a serde failure or a `normalize` error such as watch-without-cwd) and nothing logs it, so the operator sees only `pending: true`; the comment shows parking is deliberate, but dropping the reason silently is the same gap `apply_one` has in actor_config.rs:240.

claim: `reached_spec(...).ok()` drops the rebuild error, so everything parks and the operator sees pending fields with no logged reason.
reason: When `reached_spec` fails, `.ok()` at actor_config.rs:240 discards its error string (for example the normalize error that `watch` needs a `cwd`), and `park_all` then parks every field. The only refusal text is pushed under `parked_failed`, so a successful park-all logs and reports nothing: the operator sees pending fields and no reason why.

claim: `adoptable_child("trap '' TERM; sleep 300")` leaves the child running for up to 300s if the test fails before the kill ladder runs.
reason: `adoptable_child` only returns a bare pid, with no drop guard or process-group kill, so if `flock_until` panics before the drain ladder's SIGKILL lands, the TERM-ignoring `sleep 300` is orphaned for up to five minutes; the nulled stdio prevents a hang but not the leaked process.

claim: `adoptable_child` drops the `std::process::Child` without `wait`, so any test that fails before adopting leaves a zombie until the test binary exits.
reason: The claim is accurate: `adoptable_child` at `crates/shep-daemon/src/supervisor/tests/mod.rs:972` returns only `.id()` and drops the `Child` on purpose, so the adopted flock's reaper collects the exit status; if a case panics before adopting, nothing waits on the pid and it sits as a zombie until the test binary exits. The impact is small, since that zombie lasts only as long as the test binary. The bigger leak is the still-running child itself, for example the TERM-ignoring `sleep 300` in `adopt_swap.rs:476`.

claim: `let _ = t.await` discards the `JoinError`, so a panic in one of the eight `stop` tasks is swallowed; `:274` and `:284` discard their results the same way.
reason: At :251, `let _ = t.await` discards both the `JoinError` and the inner `stop` `Result`, so a panic or error in any of the eight stop tasks goes unnoticed and the test still passes; the similar discards at :274 and :284 are inside detached flood tasks, where ignoring the result is arguably intentional, so they are weaker instances.

claim: `reached_spec(...).ok()` discards the error the same way
reason: Dropping the error is deliberate and commented: a `reached_spec` failure means the app needs a restart, so `next_spec.is_none()` parks the whole config (`park_all`), the same way `apply_one` handles it. The only other ways it can fail are serde round-trips of an `AppConfig` it already holds, which can't realistically error.

claim: `adoptable_child` drops the `std::process::Child` without `wait` or `kill`; a case that fails before adoption leaves the `/bin/sh` and its `sleep 30` running, and the shell stays a zombie until the test binary exits
reason: `adoptable_child` returns only `.id()` and drops the `Child` on purpose (its doc comment says so), so no guard kills or reaps it: a case that panics before the supervisor adopts the pid leaves `/bin/sh` and its `sleep 30`/`sleep 300` running, and the shell stays a zombie until the test binary exits, since nothing else waits on it.

claim: `let _ = waiter.send(body)` loses the child's reply when the action task already gave up, so the caller sees `TimedOut` although the child answered
reason: The waiter's receiver is only gone once the action task's timeout has already fired, so the reply really did arrive after the deadline and `TimedOut` is correct; discarding the failed send is the intended late-reply drop documented on `ActionWaits::answer`.

claim: `with_count(&parked, achieved).unwrap_or(parked)` silently keeps the stale parked instance count on failure (`:197` skips the update silently), which the adjacent comment says is drift that never clears
reason: The fallback is silent and does leave a stale parked count, but `with_count` fails only when `normalize` rejects the parked config at the new count, and the code does not show whether that can happen when `stored` already normalized at the same count, or whether keeping the old count is the intended fallback.

claim: `reached_spec(...).ok()` throws away the error and parks the whole config with no log line
reason: Dropping the error is deliberate: the comment at lines 236-239 says a normalize failure from a field subset should park rather than refuse, and the outcome is still reported to the caller because every field comes back as `pending` (lines 380-395), though the specific error text is lost.

claim: `try_send(...).is_err()` drops the error and reports a merely full signal queue as `SignalOutcome::NotRunning`
reason: The comment right there shows this is on purpose: a full queue means the sheep task is too busy dying to drain syscall-fast signals, so NotRunning is the intended answer, and try_send avoids parking the actor loop.

claim: `extra_restart` discards the send error, so a memory or liveness restart request vanishes without trace when the actor is gone
reason: A send only fails once the supervisor actor has stopped, and then no sheep is left to restart; the docs and tests say this fire-and-forget, no-reply behavior is intended, so dropping the error loses nothing.

claim: `let _ = actor_tx.send(Msg::Exited ...)` (also `:108`) drops the only exit report if the actor is gone, so the exit outcome is lost
reason: `mpsc::Sender::send` fails only when the actor's receiver has been dropped, so the supervisor has already shut down and there is nothing left to record the exit outcome.

claim: `let _ = ctl.try_send(SheepCtl::Kill { grace })` discards `Full` and `Closed` after `slot.manual` was already set; benign only if a `Msg::Exited` is guaranteed to follow
reason: `SheepCtl` has only one variant, `Kill`, so `Full` means a `Kill` is already queued and that ladder will end in an exit. `Closed` means the sheep task has already ended, and its `Msg::Exited` is already on the way. Either way an exit follows and settles `slot.manual`.

claim: the `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 30'` child (also at `:247`) is never waited on by the test; if `spawn_adopted().expect` or the `kill().expect` panics first, it and its `sleep` are left running
reason: Both tests start `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 30'` with `std::process::Command` and have no guard that kills it on unwind, so a panic in `spawn_adopted().expect` or before `kill` succeeds leaves the child running (unreaped, up to 30s); the damage is small because `sleep 30` ends on its own.

claim: `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))` turns a pump that died mid-request into a successful reopen (same at `:119` for flush); documented, and pinned by `tests/reopen.rs:207` and `:229`, but a panicking pump reads as success
reason: This is intended behaviour. The doc comments on `reopen_logs` and `flush_logs` say a dropped acknowledgement means no pump is left to reopen or flush anything, so a pump that is already gone has nothing to report. Tests pin that behaviour. A panicking pump would be a separate bug in the pump, and one that shows up elsewhere, not a mistake in this ack handling.

claim: `let _ = t.await` discards both the `JoinError` and the eight stop results, so the timing assertion cannot see a panicked or failed stop
reason: The test's job is to check that sheep b's exit is processed while sheep a's kill ladder is running, and `seen_at` is captured before the tasks are joined, so a failed or panicked stop cannot change that measurement; eight concurrent stops on one sheep may also legitimately return mixed results, so ignoring them looks deliberate rather than a defect.

claim: `write_all(...).unwrap()` (and `:146`) sits in a detached pump task; a panic drops `done`, which `flush_logs` reads as `Ok(())`, so the I/O error surfaces only through a later assertion
reason: The unwraps at flush.rs:146/:153 run inside a detached `tokio::spawn`, so a panic there just drops `done`, and `flush_logs` (logs.rs:119, `ack.await.unwrap_or(Ok(()))`) reads that as success; the I/O error then shows up only indirectly, when the later `out_file.exists()` assertion fails with a misleading message.

claim: flood tasks discard `h.stop(...)` (and `:284` `h.list_checked()`); intentional for a deadlock probe, but a failure in them is invisible
reason: The test probes only for deadlock, and the Stop-event timeout assertion covers that; concurrent stop/list calls racing a kill ladder are expected to return errors, so discarding their results is intentional and hides nothing the test claims to check.

claim: `let _ = tx.send(...)` (also `:18`, `:21`) drops the reply when the caller is gone; deliberate, low
reason: These are oneshot reply senders, and a send fails only when the requesting caller has already dropped its receiver, so there is nobody left to reply to and dropping the result is the correct idiom, not a defect.

claim: `let _ = handle.start(...)` (also `:153` for `restart`) discards results in the proptest, so a wrongly failing command never reaches the invariants
reason: The proptest checks state invariants, not command success. Scripted spawn failures, readiness-gate timeouts and restarting an empty flock all make `start` and `restart` return `Err` legitimately, so the results are deliberately dropped (only `stop` and `delete` have replies whose contents the test can assert on). Any state a wrongly failing command leaves behind is still checked against the invariants after every step.

claim: `let _ = terminal.draw(...)` discards the draw error, then clears `dirty` and stamps `last_draw`. A broken tty or backend gives a frozen screen with no report and no exit.
reason: At line 167, `let _ = terminal.draw(...)` throws away the io::Result, and the code then clears `dirty` and sets `last_draw` either way; no other path reports or exits on a draw failure, so a broken backend leaves the last frame frozen on screen and nothing is reported.

claim: `handle.await.ok().flatten()` turns a panicked reveal task into "no value". The same happens for `secrets.rs:174`, where `secrets::get(...).ok().flatten()` turns an unreadable store into "no value". The operator cannot tell a failed read from a missing slot.
reason: Both collapses are deliberate and documented: the comment at ui_event_loop.rs:358-362 says a join failure reads as no value on purpose, and the `stored_value` doc at secrets.rs:160-161 lists "the store will not read" as a `None` case, so this is a design choice rather than an unintended loss of the error.

claim: a key-source `Some(Err(_))` is discarded and permanently retires the keyboard arm, with no notice. The dashboard keeps drawing but no key, `q` included, is read again, so only SIGTERM ends it.
reason: `keys_done` is set at `crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/ui_event_loop.rs:192` and nothing else reads it: no quit, no status line and no log entry follows, while the link and heartbeat arms keep redrawing, so after a key-source error or end nothing (`q` or Ctrl-C in raw mode) can exit, only SIGTERM can.

claim: `Err(_other) => Ok(())` (and `Err(RequestError::Closed)` at :225) drops every failed `ListFlock` poll without telling the UI. A shepherd that keeps refusing polls leaves a stale flock on screen with no banner.
reason: `reconcile` (link.rs:215-227) throws away every error except `Closed` and sends the UI nothing, and the UI has no age or staleness check on `Msg::Snapshot` (update.rs:48), so a live connection whose `ListFlock` keeps failing (timeouts, error replies) leaves the old flock on screen with no banner. Only a dead subscription triggers the reconnect path.

claim: `section.parse::<toml::Table>().ok()...unwrap_or_default()` turns a malformed dog section into an empty value map. The pane then shows every field as unset, which reads as defaults, and no error is surfaced.
reason: The section comes from the daemon's `dog_section` (crates/shep-daemon/src/dogs/config.rs:31). That function parses `dogs.toml` with `DogsConfig::load` and returns a `DogError::Config` when the file is malformed, and otherwise sends back a section re-rooted from an already-parsed document, so the pane only ever gets valid TOML or an empty string and the `unwrap_or_default` fallback can't hide a real parse error.

claim: a failed `serde_json::to_value(config)` becomes an empty map through `.ok()...unwrap_or_default()`. The sheep config pane and the read-only listing then render as if nothing were configured.
reason: `config` is an `AppConfig` that was just deserialized from wire JSON, and its derived `Serialize` has string keys, so `serde_json::to_value` cannot fail in practice; the empty-map fallback is dead defensive code, not a reachable misrender.

claim: the `spawn_blocking` closures for WriteSetting (also :326, :452, :488) take a `shep.toml` or `secrets.json` lock with no deadline, and the loop drops their handles on quit. `entry.rs:96` then drops the multi-thread runtime, which waits on blocking threads, so a lock held by another process hangs shep after the terminal is restored. These are blocking tasks, not child processes.
reason: The code comments themselves say `try_edit` and `secrets.json.lock` block with no deadline. The runtime built at `entry.rs:52` is dropped when `main` returns, with no `shutdown_timeout` or `shutdown_background` anywhere, and tokio's `Runtime` drop waits for running `spawn_blocking` tasks. So a lock held by another process keeps shep from exiting after lookout quits.

claim: `_ => Control::Allowed` swallows any error reading `kv.json`, so a failed read fails open to full control even when `lookout.allow_control` was set to false. The doc comment admits it.
reason: The fail-open on an unreadable kv.json is a deliberate design choice documented in resolve_control's doc comment ("the gate stops an accident, not an attacker"), so it is intended behavior rather than a defect.

claim: `let _ = msgs.send(Msg::Retrying { .. })` ignores a closed UI channel. After the UI is gone the link task keeps re-dialling for up to five more rungs instead of returning.
reason: `run_link` throws away the `Err` from `msgs.send(Msg::Retrying { attempt })` at link.rs:116, so once the UI receiver closes, each failed dial just sleeps and dials again until `attempt > RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS`; the loop never returns early, unlike the `Relinked` send and the `UiGone` path, which both do.

claim: `Terminate::install().ok()` silently drops a failed SIGTERM handler install, so the loop runs with no signal handling and says nothing.
reason: The drop is a deliberate fallback, not a lost error. `Terminate::install` fails only if the OS refuses to register a handler, which almost never happens. Without the handler the loop still quits from the keyboard: in raw mode Ctrl-C arrives as a key. And while the TUI owns the screen there is nowhere to report the failure without corrupting the display, so `.ok()` making `sigterm` an `Option` is a reasonable choice.

claim: `let _ = copy_to_clipboard(..)` discards the stdout write error. This is documented as deliberate, but a failed write is still reported as sent.
reason: The "sent" status is set in the app before the effect runs, and `copy_to_clipboard` errors are thrown away at ui_event_loop.rs:509, so a failed stdout write still says "sent" even though the escape sequence never left the process (the comment's "sent, not arrived" wording only covers a terminal that ignores OSC 52, not a failed write).

claim: `read_to_string(...).ok()` plus `is_ok_and(...)` reads an unreadable or invalid `shep.toml` as `allow_read = false`. Reveal is refused with no reason shown.
reason: Treating a missing or unreadable shep.toml as `allow_read = false` is a documented, deliberate fail-closed choice (secrets.rs:71-73, mirroring `whistle::gate::resolve_control`), and a reason is shown: the refusal notice and the pane chrome both name `[secrets] allow_read = false in shep.toml`, though neither says the file failed to parse.

claim: `let _ = requests.try_send(Sent::Lambs { id })` (and `polls.try_send` at :232) discards both `Full` and `Closed`. This is documented, but a closed channel is indistinguishable from a full one.
reason: Both sends treat a closed channel as harmless on purpose: the comment at :228–231 says a closed poll channel means the link has ended, and the reducer already handles that by refusing `r` once the link is `Lost`, so a lost lamb fetch just shows as "not read yet" and nothing downstream needs to tell `Full` apart from `Closed`.

claim: the dog schema probe runs a child through `ask_schema`. The direct child is killed and reaped at `commands/dogs/vet/mod.rs:274`. A descendant that calls `setsid` escapes the group kill and is never reaped, which `vet/mod.rs:288` documents. I found no other child-process spawn under lookout.
reason: The lookout schema probe goes through `ask_schema`, which kills only the probe's process group (`kill_probe_tree` at vet/mod.rs:274) and waits on the direct child, so a descendant that calls `setsid` survives; this is a documented limitation, not an unknown bug, and "never reaped" is slightly off because the orphan is re-parented to launchd/init rather than becoming lookout's zombie.

claim: `restore()` discards all three terminal-restore errors. This is intentional, since it runs from a panic hook and is idempotent.
reason: The discards are deliberate and documented at term.rs:25-27: `restore()` runs from a panic hook and must be best-effort and idempotent, so returning early on an error would skip the remaining restore steps.

claim: `let _ = terminal.draw(..)` drops the draw error, and `dirty`/`last_draw` are then updated as if it had worked. A dead tty (EIO) leaves the loop running blind with no notice and no exit.
reason: At line 167 the draw error is dropped with `let _ =` and `dirty`/`last_draw` are updated anyway; a dead tty also only sets `keys_done = true` without breaking, so only the SIGTERM arm can end the loop, and it keeps running on the link and heartbeat arms unless the default SIGHUP kills the process first.

claim: `resolve_control` turns any `kv::get` error into `Control::Allowed`. An unreadable `kv.json` silently turns the `lookout.allow_control false` gate off.
reason: The behaviour is real but intentional: the doc comment at crates/shep-cli/src/lookout/entry.rs:147-153 says an unreadable kv.json leaves control on, because the gate is meant to stop accidents rather than attackers, so this is a documented fail-open design choice, not a bug.

claim: the only guard held across an `.await` is the test's `Flock` in `the_loop_keeps_running_while_a_settings_write_is_stuck`, and that is deliberate. No production code under lookout holds a lock or guard across an `.await`. The only lock use is a test-only `std::sync::Mutex` in `link.rs:636`, which is not held across an await either.
reason: Under lookout, the only lock guard that lives across an `.await` is the test's deliberate `Flock` in `the_loop_keeps_running_while_a_settings_write_is_stuck`; the only other guard is term.rs's `RestoreGuard`, which restores the terminal and is not a lock, and there is no Mutex or RwLock anywhere in lookout, so the `link.rs:636` mention points outside this directory.

claim: `Terminate::install().ok()` discards a SIGTERM-handler failure silently. SIGTERM then kills the process on the default action, so the `RestoreGuard` never runs and the shell is left in raw mode.
